3.
Monodromic Soergel Bimodules

A foundational tool for working with the Elias–Williamson diagrammatic category is the Soergel functor

(3.0.1)

\mathcal{D}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W)\to\textbf{BS}\textnormal{Bim}(\mathfrak{h},W)

from the diagrammatic Hecke category to Bott–Samelson bimodules.
For finite Coxeter groups, sufficiently nice realizations over
\mathbbm{k}
, and certain small primes being invertible in
\mathbbm{k}
, this functor is an equivalence of categories.
Problems quickly arise when any of these three constraints are removed. For our later applications, it will be crucial to have a well-behaved version of (
3.0.1
) which works for arbitrary
W
and
\mathbbm{k}
.
Fortunately, a solution to this problem already exists. In
[
Abe21
]
, Abe had the ingenious idea to modify the category of Bott–Samelson bimodules by keeping track of certain localization data.
The resulting category
\mathcal{A}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W)
of Abe–Bott–Samelson bimodules gives a bimodule-theoretic incarnation of the Elias–Williamson category. In particular, by
[
Abe21
]
, there is an equivalence of categories

(3.0.2)

\mathcal{D}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}\mathcal{A}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W).

The goal of this section is to construct a monodromic version of Abe–Bott–Samelson bimodules.

3.1.
Abe–Soergel Theory

We will closely follow the approach of
[
Abe21
]
,
[
Abe24
]
, and
[
RV24
]
. The main difference between our presentation and that of
loc. cit.
will be a 2-categorical enrichment which keeps track of monodromy parameters.

Fix a Coxeter system
(W,S)
, a set of monodromy parameters
\mathfrak{o}
, and a reflection-balanced reflection-stable Abe realization
\mathfrak{h}
of
W
.

We denote
R
for the symmetric algebra of
\mathfrak{h}^{*}
over
\mathbbm{k}
.
We view
R
as a
\mathbb{Z}
-graded
\mathbbm{k}
-algebra where
\mathfrak{h}^{*}
is concentrated in degree 2.
Consider the localized ring

Q\coloneq R\left[\frac{1}{\alpha_{w}}\colon w\in\mathcal{R}(W)\right].

The roots
\alpha_{w}
are well-defined by Lemma
2.2.29
.
The ring
Q
is naturally
\mathbb{Z}
-graded. Moreover, the
W
-action on
\mathfrak{h}^{*}
induces actions on
R
and on
Q
by graded algebra automorphisms.

3.1.1.
The Category
\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/}^{\prime}

We can define a collection of 1-categories
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
whose objects are triples

(M,(M_{Q}^{w})_{w\in W},\xi_{M})

such that

(1)

M
is a graded
R
-bimodule;

(2)

each
M_{Q}^{w}
is a graded
(R,Q)
-bimodule such that
m\cdot f=w(f)\cdot m
for all
m\in M_{Q}^{w}
and
f\in R
;

(3)

M_{Q}^{w}=0
if
w\notin{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
and is only nonzero for finitely many
w\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
;

(4)

\xi_{M}:M_{Q}\coloneq M\otimes_{R}Q\to\bigoplus_{w\in W}M_{Q}^{w}
is an isomorphism of graded
(R,Q)
-bimodules.

A morphism in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
from
(M,(M_{Q}^{w})_{w\in W},\xi_{M})
to
(N,(N_{Q}^{w})_{w\in W},\xi_{N})
is a morphism of
R
-bimodules
1
1

1

We allow for morphisms of
R
-bimodules which are not just concentrated in degree 0.

\varphi:M\to N
such that

(\xi_{N}\circ(\varphi\otimes_{R}Q)\circ\xi_{M}^{-1})(M_{Q}^{w})\subset N_{Q}^{w}

for any
w\in W
. For simplicity, we often abuse notation and only write
M
instead of the triple
(M,(M_{Q}^{w})_{w\in W},\xi_{M})
.

There are bifunctors,

(3.1.1)

(-)\otimes_{R}(-):\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})\times\>_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})\to\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})

induced from the tensor product of underlying graded
R
-bimodules. These bifunctors are suitably associative and there is a unit object
R_{e}
with underlying graded bimodule
R
.
This tensor product allows us to assemble a 2-category
\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
as follows:

(1)

The object set of
\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
is
\mathfrak{o}
.

(2)

The morphism categories are defined by
\Hom_{\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})}(\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime})=\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
. The composition of morphism categories is by the tensor product (
3.1.1
)

The triple
(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
will sometimes be omitted from
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
and
\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
.

The category
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
inherits a grading shift automorphism,

(n):\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})\to\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o}),

for each
n\in\mathbb{Z}
given by
M(n)^{i}=M^{n+i}
for all
i\in\mathbb{Z}
.

3.1.2.
The Category
\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/}

For each
\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\in\mathfrak{o}
, we consider a full subcategory
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
of
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
consisting of triples
(M,(M_{Q}^{w})_{w\in W},\xi_{M})

such that
M
is finitely generated as an
R
-bimodule and flat as a right
R
-module. Note that the grading shift
(1)
preserves
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
.

Lemma 3.1.3

(
[
Abe21
, Lemma 2.6]
)
.

If
(M,(M_{Q}^{w})_{w\in W},\xi_{M})\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
, then
M
is finitely generated as a left
R
-module and as a right
R
-module.

Let
M\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
. Assume that
M
is graded free as a left
R
-module. By Lemma
3.1.3
, it must also be finitely generated.
As a result, we may define the
graded rank
of
M
, denoted
\textnormal{rank}^{\mathbb{Z}}(M)\in\mathbb{Z}[v^{\pm}]
, as the polynomial such that
M\cong R^{\oplus\textnormal{rank}^{\mathbb{Z}}(M)}
.
Note, by definition
R^{\oplus v^{n}}
should be interpreted as
R(n)
.

Lemma
3.1.3
implies that if
M\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
and
N\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
, then
M\otimes_{R}N\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
.
As a result, we can define a sub-2-category
\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
of
\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
whose morphisms categories are given by
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
.
The tuple
(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
will sometimes be omitted from
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
and
\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
.

Lemma 3.1.4
.

Suppose the realization
\mathfrak{h}
is a faithful
W
-representation. Then the forgetful functor

\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})\to R\textnormal{-bim}

is fully faithful.

Proof.

It is clear that the forgetful functor is always faithful. The content of the lemma is that it is also full.
Let
M\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
.
Define a sub
(R,Q)
-bimodule,

\underline{M}_{Q}^{w}\coloneq\{m\in M\otimes_{R}Q\mid f\cdot m=m\cdot w(f)\text{ for all }f\in R\}.

We claim that the restriction of
\xi_{M}
given by
\underline{M}_{Q}^{w}\to\bigoplus_{x\in W}M_{Q}^{x}\twoheadrightarrow M_{Q}^{w}
is an isomorphism.
It is clear that
\underline{M}_{Q}^{w}\to M_{Q}^{w}
is surjective. Let
m\in\underline{M}_{Q}^{w}
and write
\xi_{M}(m)=\sum_{x\in W}m_{x}
with
m_{x}\in M_{Q}^{x}
.
We claim that if
x\neq w
, then
m_{x}=0
. For all
f\in R
, we must have that
w(f)\cdot m_{x}=m_{x}\cdot f=x(f)\cdot m_{x}
.
On the other hand,
M_{Q}^{x}
is a free
R
-module, so this can only happen if either
w(f)=x(f)
or
m_{x}=0
. Since
\mathfrak{h}
is a faithful
W
-representation, we deduce that
m_{x}=0
, and hence
\underline{M}_{Q}^{w}\to M_{Q}^{w}
is an isomorphism.

Let
M,N\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
and let
\varphi:M\to N
be a morphism of underlying
R
-bimodules.
It is clear from the
R
-bimodules structure that
\varphi(\underline{M}_{Q}^{w})\subseteq\underline{N}_{Q}^{w}
for all
w\in W
.
The previous paragraph then tells us that
\varphi
is actually a morphism in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
.
∎

3.1.5.
Support of Bimodules

Let
M\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
.
Denote by
\zeta_{M}:M\to\bigoplus_{w\in W}M_{Q}^{w}
the composition
M\to M\otimes_{R}Q\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\xi_{M}}}{{\to}}\bigoplus_{w\in W}M_{Q}^{w}
.
Note that
\zeta_{M}
is injective since
M
is flat as a right
R
-module and since
R\hookrightarrow Q
is injective.
For each
I\subset W
, define a map
\pi_{M}^{I}:M\to\bigoplus_{w\in I}M_{Q}^{w}
via the composition
M\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\zeta_{M}}}{{\to}}\bigoplus_{w\in W}M_{Q}^{w}\twoheadrightarrow\bigoplus_{w\in I}M_{Q}^{w}.

For each
m\in M
, we will write
m_{I}\coloneq\pi_{M}^{I}(m)\in\bigoplus_{w\in I}M_{Q}^{w}
.
If
I=\{w\}
, we will simplify the notation to
\pi_{M}^{w}=\pi_{M}^{\{w\}}
and
m_{w}=m_{\{w\}}
.

We define the
support
of
M
by

\supp_{W}(M)\coloneq\{w\in W\mid M_{Q}^{w}\neq 0\}.

Similarly, we define the support of
m\in M
by

\supp_{W}(m)\coloneq\{w\in W\mid m_{w}\neq 0\}.

It is clear from the definitions that both
\supp_{W}(M)
and
\supp_{W}(m)
are subsets of
{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
.
The support of a bimodule is compatible with tensor products in the following sense:

(3.1.2)

\supp_{W}(M\otimes_{R}N)=\{xy\mid x\in\supp_{W}(M),y\in\supp_{W}(N)\}.

For
I\subset W
, let
M_{I}=\zeta_{M}^{-1}\left(\bigoplus_{w\in W}M_{Q}^{w}\right)\subseteq M
and
M^{I}=\pi_{M}^{I}(M)\subseteq\bigoplus_{w\in I}M_{Q}^{w}
.
If
I=\{w\}
, we will simplify the notation,
M_{w}=M_{\{w\}}
and
M^{w}=M^{\{w\}}
. Note that
M_{I}=\{m\in M\mid\supp_{W}(m)\subset I\}
.

We recall some standard facts about
M_{I}
and
M^{I}
that follow from the same arguments given in
[
Abe21
, §2.2]
.

Lemma 3.1.6
.

Let
I\subseteq W
and
M,N\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
such that
\supp_{W}(N)\subset I
.

(1)

The bimodules
M_{I}
and
M^{I}
are both objects in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}
such that
(M_{I})_{Q}=(M^{I})_{Q}=\bigoplus_{w\in I}M_{Q}^{w}
.

(2)

There are natural isomorphisms

\Hom_{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}}(M,N)\cong\Hom_{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}}(M^{I},N),

\Hom_{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}}(N,M)\cong\Hom_{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}}(N,M_{I}).

3.2.
Bott–Samelson Bimodules

Let
w\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
. We first define the
standard bimodule

R_{w}\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}w}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
as follows. As a left
R
-module,
R_{w}=R
and the right
R
-module structure is given by
m\cdot f=w(f)\cdot m
for
m\in R_{w}
and
f\in R
.
The localization data for
R_{w}
is given by

(R_{w})_{Q}^{x}=\begin{cases}Q_{w}&x=w,\\
0&x\neq w,\end{cases}

where
Q_{w}=R_{w}\otimes_{R}Q
.

For
w\in W
, we write
R^{w}=\{r\in R\mid w(r)=r\}
for the subring of
w
-invariants.
Suppose that
s\in W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ}
is an endosimple reflection. Fix
\delta_{s}\in\mathfrak{h}^{*}
such that
\langle\alpha_{s}^{\vee},\delta_{s}\rangle=1
. Note that
\delta_{s}
exists by Demazure surjectivity on the restricted realization for
W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ}
.
We consider the
R
-bimodule
C_{s}=R\otimes_{R^{s}}R(1)
.
The
R
-bimodule
C_{s}
can be upgraded to an object in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
by setting

(3.2.1)

(C_{s})_{Q}^{e}=(\delta_{s}\otimes 1-1\otimes s(\delta_{s}))\cdot Q,\qquad\qquad(C_{s})_{Q}^{s}=(\delta_{s}\otimes 1-1\otimes\delta_{s})\cdot Q,

and
(C_{s})_{Q}^{w}=0
for all
w\notin\{e,s\}
. The fact that this localization data actually defines an object in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}}
is routine (cf.,
[
EW16
, Claim 3.11]
).

Let
s\in S
. We define an object
B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}s}
as follows:

B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}=\begin{cases}C_{s}&\mathcal{L}s=\mathcal{L},\\
R_{s}&\mathcal{L}s\neq\mathcal{L}.\end{cases}

For an expression
\underline{w}=(s_{1},\ldots,s_{k})
with
\mathcal{L}^{\prime}=\mathcal{L}\underline{w}
, we define the Bott–Samelson bimodule in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
associated to
\underline{w}
by

B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}:=B_{s_{1}}^{\mathcal{L}}\otimes_{R}B_{s_{2}}^{\mathcal{L}s_{1}}\otimes_{R}\ldots\otimes_{R}B_{s_{k}}^{\mathcal{L}s_{1}\ldots s_{k-1}}.

Since
B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
, we have a decomposition
B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}\otimes_{R}Q\cong\bigoplus_{x\in W}(B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}})_{Q}^{x}
.
We set
B_{\underline{w},Q}^{x,\mathcal{L}}\coloneq(B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}})_{Q}^{x}
.
For a fixed
x\in W
, we also write
\pi_{\underline{w}}^{x}\coloneq\pi_{B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}}^{x}
. Similarly, for
I\subseteq W
, we write
B_{\underline{w},I}^{\mathcal{L}}\coloneq(B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}})_{I}
and
B_{\underline{w}}^{I,\mathcal{L}}\coloneq(B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}})^{I}

We can then define a full replete subcategory
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
of
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
generated by objects of the form

B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}:=B_{s_{1}}^{\mathcal{L}}\otimes_{R}\ldots\otimes_{R}B_{s_{k}}^{\mathcal{L}s_{1}\ldots s_{k-1}}

where
\underline{w}=(s_{1},\ldots,s_{k})\in\Exp(W)
such that
\mathcal{L}\underline{w}=\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
.
The category
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
is called the category of
(\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime})
-monodromic Bott–Samelson bimodules
.

We also will consider the full subcategory
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
of
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
which is the additive hull of
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
.
When
\mathbbm{k}
is a complete local ring, we will denote by
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
the full subcategory of
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
given by taking the idempotent completion of
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
.
The category
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
is called the category of
(\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime})
-monodromic Soergel bimodules
.
It is a standard fact about additive categories over complete local rings that
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
is Krull–Schmidt (cf.,
[
Ach21
, Example A.8.6]
).

We can assemble these 1-categories into wide sub-2-categories of
\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
. These are defined as follows:

(1)

\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
whose morphism categories are the
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
’s;

(2)

\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
whose morphism categories are the
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
’s;

(3)

if
\mathbbm{k}
is a complete local ring,
\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
whose morphism categories are the
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
’s.

As mentioned for
\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
, we will sometimes drop the tuple
(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
from the notation in all of these 2-categories and their morphism categories.

Lemma 3.2.1
.

Let
\underline{w}\in\Exp(W)
.
The module
B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}
is graded free as a left (resp. right)
R
-module with graded rank
(v+v^{-1})^{\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w})}
.

Proof.

Let
s\in S
. If
\mathcal{L}s=\mathcal{L}
, then
B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}\cong R(-1)\oplus R(1)
as left (resp. right)
R
-modules.
If
\mathcal{L}s\neq\mathcal{L}
, then
B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}\cong R
as a left (resp. right)
R
-module.
The result then follows from induction on the length of
\underline{w}
by taking tensor products.
∎

Lemma 3.2.2
.

(1)

Let
x,y\in W
. There is a unique isomorphism in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}xy}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
,

R_{x}\otimes_{R}R_{y}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}R_{xy},

taking
1\otimes 1
to
1
.

(2)

Let
w\in W
and
s\in S
such that
\mathcal{L}ws=\mathcal{L}w
and
\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(w)=0
.
There are unique isomorphisms in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
,

R_{w}\otimes_{R}C_{s}\otimes_{R}R_{w^{-1}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}C_{wsw^{-1}},

taking
1\otimes 1\otimes 1\otimes 1
to
1\otimes 1
.

Proof.

Statement (1) follows directly from definitions.

For statement (2), the conditions on
w
and
s
ensure that
wsw^{-1}
is an endosimple reflection in
W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ}
.
Consider the morphism of
\mathbbm{k}
-bimodules,

(3.2.2)

\varphi:R_{w}\otimes R_{w^{-1}}\to R\otimes_{R^{wsw^{-1}}}R,\qquad\qquad a\otimes b\mapsto a\otimes w(b).

We can first check that
\varphi
is a morphism of
R
-bimodules.
The left
R
-linearity is obvious. For the right
R
-linearity, we can compute

\varphi(a\otimes bw^{-1}(r))=a\otimes w(bw^{-1}(r))=a\otimes w(b)

for
a\in R_{w},b\in R_{w^{-1}},r\in R
. Next, we will show that
\varphi
is
R^{s}
-balanced.
Let
f\in R^{s}
. Mote that there is a ring morphism
R^{s}\to R^{wsw^{-1}}
given by
f\mapsto w(f)
, i.e.,
w(f)
is
wsw^{-1}
-invariant.
Hence,

\varphi(aw(f)\otimes b)=aw(f)\otimes w(b)=a\otimes w(fb)=\varphi(a\otimes fb).

As a result, there is an induced morphism of
R
-bimodules

\overline{\varphi}:R_{w}\otimes_{R^{s}}R_{w^{-1}}\to R\otimes_{R^{wsw^{-1}}}R.

It is easy to check that as left
R
-modules, both
R_{w}\otimes_{R^{s}}R_{w^{-1}}
and
R\otimes_{R^{wsw^{-1}}}R
are free
R
-modules of rank 2.
Moreover, since
w\cdot(-):R\to R
takes
s
-(anti)invariants to
wsw^{-1}
-(anti)invariants, it is easy to check that
\overline{\varphi}
is in fact an isomorphism of
R
-bimodules.
We then have an isomorphism of
R
-bimodules

R_{w}\otimes_{R}C_{s}\otimes_{R}R_{w^{-1}}\cong R_{w}\otimes_{R^{s}}R_{w^{-1}}(1)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\overline{\varphi}}}{{\to}}R\otimes_{R^{wsw^{-1}}}R(1)=C_{wsw^{-1}}.

Clearly, this isomorphism takes
1\otimes 1\otimes 1\otimes 1
to
1\otimes 1
. Since the degree 0 endomorphism algebra of bimodule morphisms is rank 1, the isomorphism is uniquely determined.
∎

Lemma 3.2.3
.

Let
s\in S
. The functor
(-)\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}:\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})\to\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
is biadjoint to
(-)\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}:\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})\to\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
.

Proof.

When
\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s=\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
, this is proved in
[
Abe21
, Lemma 2.15]
.
If
\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s\neq\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
, then there is an isomorphism
B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}\cong R
.
As a result
(-)\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
, is an equivalence of categories with inverse
(-)\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}
, in particular the functors are biadjoint.
∎

3.2.4.
Duality

Let
M\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
. Define

D(M)\coloneq\Hom_{R\textnormal{-mod}}(M,R)\qquad\text{and}\qquad D(M)_{Q}^{w}\coloneq\Hom_{Q\textnormal{-mod}}(M_{Q}^{w},Q).

The
R
-bimodule structure on
D(M)
is given by
(rfs)(m)=f(rms)
for
r,s\in R
,
m\in M
, and
f\in D(M)
.
It is easy to check that
D(M)
is well-defined in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
(cf.,
[
Abe21
, §2.6]
).
Moreover,
D(M)
extends to a functor

D:\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\op}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})\to\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o}).

The following lemma is a combination of results in
[
Abe21
, §2.6]
.

Lemma 3.2.5
.

Let
I\subseteq W
and
w\in W
. Let
M\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
.

(1)

There is an isomorphism
D(M^{I})\cong D(M)_{I}
.

(2)

We have that
D(M)_{w}
is graded free as a left
R
-module with graded rank

\textnormal{rank}^{\mathbb{Z}}(D(M)_{w})(v)=\textnormal{rank}^{\mathbb{Z}}(M^{w})(v^{-1}).

(3)

We have a natural isomorphism
D(D(M)_{w})\cong M^{w}
.

(4)

The functor
D
preserves
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
. Moreover, there is a natural isomorphism of functors
D^{2}\cong\id
on
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
.

Proof.

Statement (1) is
[
Abe21
, Lemma 2.18]
and Statements (2) and (3) is
[
Abe21
, Lemma 2.19]
. Statement (4) is a slight generalization of
[
Abe21
, Lemma 2.20]
. A proof of this generalized variant can be found in
[
Kan20
, Proposition 2.11]
.
∎

3.3.
Monodromic Hecke Algebroid

3.3.1.
Definitions and First Properties

We recall the monodromic Hecke algebroid introduced in
[
San25
]
based on the monodromic Hecke algebra developed by Lusztig
[
Lus16
,
Lus19
]
.

Definition 3.3.2
.

The
monodromic Hecke algebroid
of
W
with monodromy
\mathfrak{o}
, denoted by
\mathcal{H}^{\mon}(W,\mathfrak{o})
, is a
\mathbb{Z}
-linear category whose objects are elements of
\mathfrak{o}
.
We write
{}_{\mathcal{L}}\mathcal{H}^{\mon}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(W,\mathfrak{o})
for the morphism space
\Hom_{\mathcal{H}^{\mon}(W,\mathfrak{o})}(\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime})
. It is defined as the free
\mathbb{Z}[v,v^{-1}]
-module with basis
\{H_{w}^{\mathcal{L}}\}_{w\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}}
.
The composition in
\mathcal{H}^{\mon}(W,\mathfrak{o})
is defined by the generating relations

(3.3.1)

H_{x}^{\mathcal{L}}H_{s}^{\mathcal{L}x}\coloneq\begin{cases}H_{xs}^{\mathcal{L}}&xs>x,\\
(v^{-1}-v)H_{x}^{\mathcal{L}}+H_{xs}^{\mathcal{L}}&xs<x,\mathcal{L}xs=\mathcal{L}x,\\
H_{xs}^{\mathcal{L}}&xs<x,\mathcal{L}xs\neq\mathcal{L}x.\end{cases}

We define the
standard form
as the sesquilinear pairing

\langle-,-\rangle:{}_{\mathcal{L}}\mathcal{H}^{\mon}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(W,\mathfrak{o})\times{}_{\mathcal{L}}\mathcal{H}^{\mon}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(W,\mathfrak{o})\to\mathbb{Z}[v,v^{-1}]

given by the relations
\langle H_{x}^{\mathcal{L}},H_{y}^{\mathcal{L}}\rangle=\delta_{x,y}
for all
x,y\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
.
The standard form satisfies the following “biadjointness” relation: for all
x\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
,
y\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}
, and
s\in S
,

(3.3.2)

\langle H_{x}^{\mathcal{L}}H_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}},H_{y}^{\mathcal{L}}\rangle=\langle H_{x}^{\mathcal{L}},H_{y}^{\mathcal{L}}H_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}\rangle.

The
bar involution
on the monodromic Hecke algebroid is the
\mathbb{Z}
-linear functor

\overline{(-)}:\mathcal{H}^{\mon}(W,\mathfrak{o})\to\mathcal{H}^{\mon}(W,\mathfrak{o})

defined on generators by

\overline{H_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}}=\begin{cases}H_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}+(v-v^{-1})H_{e}^{\mathcal{L}}&\text{if }\mathcal{L}s=\mathcal{L},\\
H_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}&\text{if }\mathcal{L}s\neq\mathcal{L},\end{cases}

and on Laurent polynomials by
\overline{v}=v^{-1}
.

3.3.3.
Preliminary Relationship with Bimodules

For each
s\in S
, define

\underline{H}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}\coloneq\begin{cases}H_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}+vH_{e}^{\mathcal{L}}&\mathcal{L}s=\mathcal{L},\\
H_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}&\mathcal{L}s\neq\mathcal{L}.\end{cases}

More generally, if
\underline{w}=(s_{1},\ldots,s_{k})\in\Exp(W)
. We define
\underline{H}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}=H_{s_{1}}^{\mathcal{L}}\ldots H_{s_{k}}^{\mathcal{L}s_{1}\ldots s_{k-1}}
.
Furthermore, we define a collection of polynomials
p_{\underline{w}}^{x,\mathcal{L}}=\langle\underline{H}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}},H_{x}^{\mathcal{L}}\rangle\in\mathbb{Z}[v^{\pm 1}]
.
It is easy to check that

\underline{H}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}=\sum_{x\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}}p_{\underline{w}}^{x,\mathcal{L}}H_{x}^{\mathcal{L}}.

Lemma 3.3.4
.

Let
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
.
Let
\underline{w}\in\Exp(W)
be an expression for
w\in\beta
. Then

\sum_{x\in\beta}v^{\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(x)}p_{\underline{w}}^{x,\mathcal{L}}(v^{-1})=(v+v^{-1})^{\#K(\underline{w},\mathcal{L})}.

Proof.

Let
\underline{\mathbb{Z}[v,v^{-1}]}
denote the algebroid given by viewing
\mathbb{Z}[v,v^{-1}]
as an algebroid with a single object.
We define a functor
F:\mathcal{H}^{\mon}(W,\mathfrak{o})\to\underline{\mathbb{Z}[v,v^{-1}]}
by
F(H_{w}^{\mathcal{L}})=v^{-\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(w)}
.
It can be easily checked from the defining relations for the monodromic Hecke algebroid that
F
is well-defined.
Note that for
s\in S
,

F(\underline{H}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}})=\begin{cases}v+v^{-1}&\mathcal{L}s=\mathcal{L},\\
1&\mathcal{L}s\neq\mathcal{L}.\end{cases}

In particular,
F(\underline{H}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}})=(v+v^{-1})^{\#K(\underline{w},\mathcal{L})}
.
Note that
p_{\underline{w}}^{x,\mathcal{L}}=0
if
x\notin{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
.
The result then follows from applying
F
to
\underline{H}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}=\sum_{x\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}}p_{\underline{w}}^{x,\mathcal{L}}H_{x}^{\mathcal{L}}
and replacing
v
by
v^{-1}
.
∎

Lemma 3.3.5
.

Let
\underline{w}\in\Exp(W)
and
x\in W
. Then
\textnormal{rank}^{\mathbb{Z}}_{Q}(B_{\underline{w},Q}^{x,\mathcal{L}})=p_{\underline{w}}^{x,\mathcal{L}}(1)
.

Proof.

Recall the groupoid
M^{\mathfrak{o}}(W)
whose object set is
\mathfrak{o}
and whose morphism sets are given by
{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
.
Let
\mathbb{Z}[M^{\mathfrak{o}}(W)]
denote the free
\mathbb{Z}
-algebroid over
M^{\mathfrak{o}}(W)
.
We can define the specialization functor

(-)_{v=1}:\mathcal{H}^{\mon}(W,\mathfrak{o})\to\mathbb{Z}[M^{\mathfrak{o}}(W)]

defined by
v\mapsto 1
and
H_{w}^{\mathcal{L}}\mapsto w\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}w}
.

We will now argue by induction on the length of
\underline{w}
.
If
\underline{w}=\varnothing
, the claim is obvious.
Suppose
\underline{w}=\underline{w}^{\prime}s
for some
s\in S
.
By applying specialization to
\underline{H}_{\underline{w}^{\prime}}^{\mathcal{L}}=\sum_{x\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}}p_{\underline{w}^{\prime}}^{x,\mathcal{L}}H_{x}^{\mathcal{L}}
and
\underline{H}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}=\sum_{x\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}}p_{\underline{w}}^{x,\mathcal{L}}H_{x}^{\mathcal{L}}
we get the relation

p_{\underline{w}}^{x,\mathcal{L}}(1)=\begin{cases}p_{\underline{w}}^{x,\mathcal{L}}(1)+p_{\underline{w}}^{xs,\mathcal{L}}(1)&s\in\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s=\mathcal{L}^{\prime},\\
p_{\underline{w}}^{xs,\mathcal{L}}(1)&\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s\neq\mathcal{L}^{\prime}.\end{cases}

On the other hand, for any
M\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}
,

(M\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s})_{Q}^{x}\cong\begin{cases}M_{Q}^{x}\oplus M_{Q}^{xs}&\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s=\mathcal{L}^{\prime},\\
M_{Q}^{xs}&\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s\neq\mathcal{L}^{\prime}.\end{cases}

As a result,
\textnormal{rank}^{\mathbb{Z}}_{Q}(B_{\underline{w},Q}^{x,\mathcal{L}})=\textnormal{rank}^{\mathbb{Z}}_{Q}((B_{\underline{w}^{\prime}}^{\mathcal{L}}\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s})_{Q}^{x})=p_{\underline{w}}^{x,\mathcal{L}}(1)
.
∎

3.4.
Morphisms of Bimodules

We will define a collection of morphisms which we will later show generate the morphism spaces of Bott–Samelson bimodules.

3.4.1.
1-Color Morphisms

Let
s\in S
such that
\mathcal{L}s=\mathcal{L}
. By Demazure surjectivity, we can find some
\delta_{s}\in\mathfrak{h}^{*}
for which
\langle\alpha_{s}^{\vee},\delta_{s}\rangle=1
.
Let
\partial_{s}:R\to R^{s}
be the
R^{s}
-module map defined by
\partial_{s}(f)=(f-s(f))/\alpha_{s}
. We use the identification
C_{s}\otimes_{R}C_{s}=R\otimes_{R^{s}}R\otimes_{R^{s}}R(2)
.
We then define morphisms of graded
R
-bimodules

\displaystyle\nu^{s}

\displaystyle:C_{s}\to C_{s}\otimes_{R}C_{s}(-1),

\displaystyle f\otimes g

\displaystyle\mapsto f\otimes 1\otimes g,

\displaystyle\epsilon^{s}

\displaystyle:C_{s}\to R(1),

\displaystyle f\otimes g

\displaystyle\mapsto fg,

\displaystyle\mu^{s}

\displaystyle:C_{s}\otimes_{R}C_{s}\to C_{s}(-1),

\displaystyle f\otimes g\otimes h

\displaystyle\mapsto\partial_{s}(g)f\otimes h,

\displaystyle\eta^{s}

\displaystyle:R\to C_{s}(1),

\displaystyle 1

\displaystyle\mapsto\delta_{s}\otimes 1-1\otimes s(\delta_{s}),

\displaystyle\cup^{s}

\displaystyle:R\to C_{s}\otimes_{R}C_{s},

\displaystyle 1

\displaystyle\mapsto\delta_{s}\otimes 1\otimes 1-1\otimes 1\otimes s(\delta_{s}),

\displaystyle\cap^{s}

\displaystyle:C_{s}\otimes_{R}C_{s}\to R,

\displaystyle f\otimes g\otimes h

\displaystyle\mapsto\partial_{s}(g)fh.

Note that
\cup^{s}=\nu^{s}\circ\eta^{s}
and
\cap^{s}=\epsilon^{s}\circ\mu^{s}
. It is straightforward (albeit tedious) to check that all the above maps are morphisms in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}}
.

Let
s\in S
such that
\mathcal{L}s\neq\mathcal{L}
. We then define morphisms of graded
R
-bimodules

\displaystyle\cup^{s}

\displaystyle:R\to R_{s}\otimes_{R}R_{s},

\displaystyle 1

\displaystyle\mapsto 1\otimes 1,

\displaystyle\cap^{s}

\displaystyle:R_{s}\otimes_{R}R_{s}\to R,

\displaystyle f\otimes g

\displaystyle\mapsto fs(g).

Likewise, these are morphisms in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}s}
.

3.4.2.
Rex Moves

For each
\underline{w}=(s_{1},\ldots,s_{k})\in\Exp(W)
, we define an element
u_{\underline{w}}=u_{1}\otimes\ldots\otimes u_{k}\in B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}
by

u_{i}=\begin{cases}u_{s_{i}}=1\otimes 1\in C_{s_{i}}&\text{if }i\in K(\underline{w},\mathcal{L}),\\
1\in R_{s_{i}}&\text{if }i\notin K(\underline{w},\mathcal{L}).\end{cases}

The element
u_{\underline{w}}
is called the
1-tensor
of
B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}
.

Let
s,t\in S
be distinct simple reflections such that
m=m_{s,t}<\infty
. We wish to construct a morphism

\beta_{s,t}:B_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to B_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}

such that
\beta_{s,t}(u_{{}_{s}\underline{m}})=u_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}
.
Unfortunately, such a map is known to only exist under constraints on the realization
\mathfrak{h}
.

Proposition 3.4.3
.

Assume that
\mathfrak{h}
is a monodromic Abe realization. There exists a morphism
\beta_{s,t}:B_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to B_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}
such that
\beta_{s,t}(u_{{}_{s}\underline{m}})=u_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}
.

Proof.

Let
W_{s,t}^{\mathcal{L}}\coloneq W_{\{s,t\}}\cap W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ}
. Let
w_{s,t}
(resp.
w_{s,t}^{\mathcal{L}}
) denote the longest element of
W_{\{s,t\}}
(resp.
W_{s,t}^{\mathcal{L}}
).
By Proposition
2.2.24
,
\mathfrak{h}
is an Abe realization for
W_{s,t}^{\mathcal{L}}

If
W_{s,t}^{\mathcal{L}}=1
, then
B_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\cong R_{w_{s,t}}\cong B_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}
.
Similarly, if
W_{s,t}^{\mathcal{L}}
has rank 1, then
B_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\cong B_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}
. As a result, in these cases the desired
\beta_{s,t}
map clearly exists.

Now suppose
W_{s,t}^{\mathcal{L}}
has rank 2 with simple generators
s^{\prime}=(st)^{k}s
and
t^{\prime}=(ts)^{\ell}t
.
Note
v\coloneq v_{s,t}^{\mathcal{L}}=m_{s^{\prime},t^{\prime}}
. By
[
Abe24
, Theorem 3.9]
, there then exists a morphism

\beta_{s^{\prime},t^{\prime}}:\underbrace{C_{s^{\prime}}\otimes_{R}C_{t^{\prime}}\otimes_{R}\ldots}_{v\text{ factors}}\longrightarrow\underbrace{C_{t^{\prime}}\otimes_{R}C_{s^{\prime}}\otimes_{R}\ldots}_{v\text{ factors}}

such that
\beta_{s^{\prime},t^{\prime}}(u_{{}_{s^{\prime}}\underline{v}})=u_{{}_{t^{\prime}}\underline{v}}
.

We can then find
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}w_{s,t}}
such that
w_{s,t}^{\mathcal{L}}w^{\beta}=w_{s,t}
. By Lemma
3.2.2
, there are isomorphisms

B_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\cong\underbrace{C_{s^{\prime}}\otimes_{R}C_{t^{\prime}}\otimes_{R}\ldots}_{v\text{ factors}}\otimes_{R}R_{w^{\beta}}\qquad\text{and}\qquad B_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\cong\underbrace{C_{t^{\prime}}\otimes_{R}C_{s^{\prime}}\otimes_{R}\ldots}_{v\text{ factors}}\otimes_{R}R_{w^{\beta}}

which take 1-tensors to 1-tensors.
We can then define
\beta_{s,t}\coloneq\beta_{s^{\prime},t^{\prime}}\otimes\id_{R_{w^{\beta}}}:B_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to B_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}
which satisfies
\beta_{s,t}(u_{{}_{s}\underline{m}})=u_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}
.
∎

More generally, if
\underline{x}
and
\underline{y}
are reduced expressions of some
w\in W
, then each path
\Gamma
in the rex graph for
w
gives rise to a morphism
\beta_{\Gamma}:B_{\underline{x}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to B_{\underline{y}}^{\mathcal{L}}

composed of the various
\beta_{s,t}
-maps.
It is clear from its construction that
\beta_{\Gamma}(u_{\underline{x}})=u_{\underline{y}}
. Of course such a morphism depends on the choice of
\Gamma
.

3.5.
Algebraic Monodromic–Endoscopic Equivalence

In this section, we will provide an equivalence between the category of monodromic Bott–Samelson bimodules and the category of Bott–Samelson bimodules for the endoscopic Coxeter group.

3.5.1.
Block Decomposition of Soergel Bimodules

Definition 3.5.2
.

Let
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
. The
\beta
-block
of
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
is the full replete subcategory
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS,\beta}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
generated by the objects
B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}
where
\underline{w}\in\Exp(W)
is an expression of
w\in\beta
.
We also define
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\oplus,\beta}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
as the additive hull of
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS,\beta}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
.

It is clear from definitions that
\otimes_{R}
preserves blocks, i.e., for
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
and
\gamma\in{}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}
, we have that

(3.5.1)

\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS,\beta}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})\otimes_{R}\>{}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}^{\BS,\gamma}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})\subset\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}^{\BS,\beta\gamma}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o}).

Lemma 3.5.3
.

Let
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
and
M\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\oplus,\beta}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
, then
\supp_{W}(M)\subseteq\beta
.

Proof.

Let
\underline{w}\in\Exp(W)
be an expression for
w\in\beta
.
We argue by induction on the length of
\underline{w}
that
\supp_{W}(B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}})\subseteq\beta
.
If
\underline{w}=\varnothing
, then the claim is obvious.
Now suppose
\underline{w}=\underline{y}s
with
\underline{y}
an expression for
ws\in\gamma
for some block
\gamma\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}
.

If
\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s=\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
, then
\beta=\gamma
.
It follows from the definitions that

(3.5.2)

B_{\underline{w},Q}^{x,\mathcal{L}}\cong B_{\underline{y},Q}^{x,\mathcal{L}}\oplus B_{\underline{y},Q}^{xs,\mathcal{L}}.

Since
\supp_{W}\left(B_{\underline{y}}^{\mathcal{L}}\right)\subseteq\gamma
and
s\in W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\circ}
, we can conclude that (
3.5.2
) is only nonzero when
x\in\beta
.

If
\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s\neq\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
, then we have
B_{\underline{w},Q}^{x,\mathcal{L}}\cong B_{\underline{y},Q}^{xs,\mathcal{L}}
.
Therefore,

\supp_{W}\left(B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}\right)=\supp_{W}(B_{\underline{y}}^{\mathcal{L}})\cdot s\subseteq\gamma\cdot s=\beta.

∎

Lemma 3.5.4
.

Let
M,N\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
such that
\supp_{W}(M)
and
\supp_{W}(N)
are disjoint. Then
\Hom_{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}}(M,N)=0
.

Proof.

Let
I=\supp_{W}(M)
.
By Lemma
3.1.6
(2), we have an isomorphism

\Hom_{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}}(M,N)\cong\Hom_{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\prime}}(M,N_{I}).

However, since
\supp_{W}(N)\cap I=\varnothing
, we have that
N_{I}=0
.
∎

Lemma 3.5.5
.

We have direct sum decompositions of additive categories

\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})=\bigoplus_{\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}}\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\oplus,\beta}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o}).

Proof.

It is clear from definitions that
\left\{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\oplus,\beta}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})\right\}_{\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}}
generate
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})
under direct sums.
It remains to show that if
\underline{x},\underline{y}\in\Exp(W)
are expressions for
x\in\beta
and
y\in\gamma
where
\beta,\gamma\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
are distinct blocks, then

(3.5.3)

\Hom_{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}}(B_{\underline{x}}^{\mathcal{L}},B_{\underline{y}}^{\mathcal{L}})=0.

The vanishing of (
3.5.3
) follows immediately from Lemmas
3.5.3
and Lemma
3.5.4
.
∎

3.5.6.
Neutral Block Endoscopy

Proposition 3.5.7
.

Let
\mathcal{L}\in\mathfrak{o}
. There is an equivalence of monoidal categories

\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}:\>_{1\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/1}^{\oplus}(W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ},\mathfrak{h},1)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}}^{\oplus,\circ}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})

such that
\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}(B_{\underline{x}})\cong B_{\underline{x}^{\prime}}^{\mathcal{L}}
where
\underline{x}^{\prime}
is an expression in
W
obtained from
\underline{x}
by replacing endosimple reflections with reduced expressions in
W
.

Proof.

Let
Q^{\prime}=R[\frac{1}{\alpha_{w}}\colon w\in\mathcal{R}(W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ})]
.
Since
\mathcal{R}(W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ})\subseteq\mathcal{R}(W)
, there is an inclusion of graded rings
Q^{\prime}\to Q
.
We can then define a functor

(3.5.4)

\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}:\>_{1\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/1}(W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ},\mathfrak{h},1)\to\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{C}_{/\mathcal{L}}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})

as follows.
Given an object
(M,M_{Q^{\prime}}^{w},\xi_{M})
, we define the underlying
R
-bimodule of
\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}(M)
to be
M
.
The localization data is given by
\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}(M)_{Q}^{w}\coloneq M_{Q^{\prime}}^{w}\otimes_{Q^{\prime}}Q
and
\xi_{\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}(M)}=\xi_{M}\otimes_{Q^{\prime}}Q
.
It is easy to check that
\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}
defines a fully faithful monoidal functor which restricts to a functor

(3.5.5)

\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}:\>_{1\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/1}^{\oplus}(W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ},\mathfrak{h},1)\to\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}}^{\oplus,\circ}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o}).

It remains to check that
\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}
is essentially surjective.
Let
\underline{w}
be an expression in
W
of an element
w\in W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ}
.
We argue by induction on
\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w})
. If
\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w})=0
, then
B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}\cong R_{e}
which is clearly in the essential image of
\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}
.
If
\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w})=k>0
, then we can write
\underline{w}=\underline{x}\underline{y}
such that
\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{x})=k-1
and
\ell_{\mathcal{L}\underline{x}}(\underline{y})=1
. Let
x
and
y
be the evaluations of
\underline{x}
and
\underline{y}
respectively.
Pick a block
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}x}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}}
such that
xw^{\beta}
is in the neutral block.
Since
w
is in the neutral block, we must also have that
w^{\beta,-1}y
is in the neutral block.
Let
\underline{v}
be a reduced expression of
w^{\beta}
.
By induction,
B_{\underline{x}\underline{v}}^{\mathcal{L}}
is in the essential image of
\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}
.
Since
\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{y})=1
and
w^{\beta,-1}y
is in the neutral block,
w^{\beta,-1}y
is an endosimple reflection. As a result,
B_{\overline{\underline{v}}\underline{y}}^{\mathcal{L}}\cong C_{w^{\beta,-1}y}
is also in the essential image.
Since
\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}
is monoidal, we then have that
B_{\underline{x}\underline{v}}^{\mathcal{L}}\otimes_{R}B_{\overline{\underline{v}}\underline{y}}^{\mathcal{L}}\cong B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}
is in the essential image.
As a result,
\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}
is essentially surjective, and hence an equivalence of categories.
∎

3.5.8.
General Endoscopy

Let
\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime},\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}\in\mathfrak{o}
,
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
, and
\gamma\in{}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}
. There is an equivalence of monoidal categories

{}^{\beta}(-):\>_{1\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/1}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\circ},1)\to\>_{1\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/1}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ},1)

induced by the isomorphism of Coxeter groups
W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\circ}\to W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ}
defined by
w\mapsto w^{\beta}ww^{\beta,-1}
.
It follows from definitions that
{}^{\beta}({}^{\gamma}(-))\cong{}^{\beta\gamma}(-)
.

On the monodromic side, there is an equivalence of monoidal categories

{}^{\beta}(-):\>_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\oplus,\circ}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})\to\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}}^{\oplus,\circ}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})

defined by
M\mapsto R_{w^{\beta}}\otimes_{R}M\otimes_{R}R_{w^{\beta,-1}}
. By Lemma
3.2.2
that
{}^{\beta}({}^{\gamma}(-))\cong{}^{\beta\gamma}(-)
.

Lemma 3.5.9
.

There are natural isomorphisms making the following diagram commute for each
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
.

(3.5.6)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\>{}_{1\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/1}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\circ},1)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\oplus,\circ}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\>{}_{1\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/1}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ},1)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}}^{\oplus,\circ}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{}^{\beta}(-)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Psi_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\alg}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{}^{\beta}(-)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}}

Moreover, these natural transformations are compatible with respect to block composition.

Proof.

After unpacking definitions and using monoidality of the maps involved in (
3.5.6
), it suffices to construct isomorphisms

\xi_{s}^{\beta}:C_{w^{\beta}sw^{\beta,-1}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}R_{w^{\beta}}\otimes_{R}C_{s}\otimes_{R}R_{w^{\beta,-1}}

for each endosimple reflection
s\in S_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\circ}
. By Lemma
3.2.2
, we can take
\xi_{s}^{\beta}
to be the unique isomorphism which preserves the 1-tensor.
This then defines a natural transformation of functors
\xi^{\beta}:\Psi_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\alg}\circ{}^{\beta}(-)\implies{}^{\beta}(-)\circ\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}
.

Let
\gamma\in{}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}
.
Since
\xi_{s}^{\beta}
is the unique map which preserves the 1-tensor, we have that

\xi_{s}^{\gamma}\circ\xi_{w^{\gamma}sw^{\gamma,-1}}^{\beta}=\xi_{s}^{\beta\gamma}
for
s\in S_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}^{\circ}
. As a result, the natural transformations
\xi^{\beta}
are compatible with respect to block composition.
∎

We will construct a 2-category
\mathcal{A}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},M^{\mathfrak{o}}(W))
, called the
endoscopic 2-category of Bott–Samelson bimodules
as follows. The object set of
\mathcal{A}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},M^{\mathfrak{o}}(W))
is
\mathfrak{o}
.
The morphism category from
\mathcal{L}
to
\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
of
\mathcal{A}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},M^{\mathfrak{o}}(W))
is given by
\bigoplus_{\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}}\mathcal{A}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},\beta)
where
\mathcal{A}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},\beta)\coloneq\>_{1\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/1}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ},1)
.
The vertical composition is induced from the composition in
\mathcal{A}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},\beta)
. Let
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
and
\gamma\in{}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}
.
We define the horizontal composition, denoted
\otimes
as the bifunctor

\displaystyle\mathcal{A}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},\beta)\times\mathcal{A}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},\gamma)

\displaystyle=\>_{1\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/1}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ},1)\times\>_{1\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/1}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\circ},1)

\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\id\times{}^{\beta}(-)}}{{\longrightarrow}}\>_{1\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/1}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ},1)\times\>_{1\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/1}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ},1)

\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\otimes_{R}}}{{\to}}\>_{1\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/1}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ},1)

\displaystyle=\mathcal{A}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},\beta\gamma).

Theorem 3.5.10

(Algebraic Monodromic-Endoscopic Equivalence)
.

There is an equivalence of 2-categories

\Psi^{\alg}:\mathcal{A}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},M^{\mathfrak{o}}(W))\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}\>_{\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})

which restricts to the equivalence of monoidal categories

\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}:\>_{1\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/1}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ},1)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})

for each
\mathcal{L}\in\mathfrak{o}
coming from Proposition
3.5.7
.

Proof.

Let
\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\in\mathfrak{o}
and
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
. On objects,
\Psi^{\alg}(\mathcal{L})=\mathcal{L}
. On morphism categories, we define
\Psi^{\alg}
as the composition

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{A}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},\beta)=\>_{1\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/1}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},W_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ},1)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}}^{\oplus,\circ}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\oplus,\beta}(\mathfrak{h},W,\mathfrak{o}).}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(-)\otimes_{R}R_{w^{\beta}}}

If we can prove that
\Psi^{\alg}
is a 2-functor, then it is automatic from Proposition
3.5.7
that it will be an equivalence of 2-categories.
Let
M\in\mathcal{A}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},\beta)
and
N\in\mathcal{A}^{\oplus}(\mathfrak{h},\gamma)
. We will construct a natural isomorphism

(3.5.7)

\Psi^{\alg}(M)\otimes_{R}\Psi^{\alg}(N)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}\Psi^{\alg}(M\otimes N)

given by the composition

\displaystyle\Psi^{\alg}(M)\otimes_{R}\Psi^{\alg}(N)

\displaystyle=\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}(M)\otimes_{R}R_{w^{\beta}}\otimes_{R}\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}(N)\otimes_{R}R_{w^{\gamma}}

\displaystyle\cong\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}(M)\otimes_{R}R_{w^{\beta}}\otimes_{R}\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}(N)\otimes_{R}R_{w^{\beta,-1}}\otimes_{R}R_{w^{\beta\gamma}}

(3.5.8)

\displaystyle\cong\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}(M)\otimes_{R}\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}({}^{\beta}N)\otimes_{R}R_{w^{\beta\gamma}}

(3.5.9)

\displaystyle\cong\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}(M\otimes_{R}{}^{\beta}N)\otimes_{R}R_{w^{\beta\gamma}}

\displaystyle=\Psi^{\alg}(M\otimes N),

where (
3.5.8
) is Lemma
3.5.9
and (
3.5.9
) comes from
\Psi_{\mathcal{L}}^{\alg}
being monoidal.
It is easy to check from the compatibility of Lemma
3.5.9
with block composition that (
3.5.7
) is associative.
Therefore, (
3.5.7
) makes
\Psi^{\alg}
into a 2-functor.
∎

4.
Algebraic Light Leaves

The goal of this section is to extend the construction of light leaves for Bott–Samelson bimodules (cf.,
[
Lib08
,
Abe21
]
) to monodromic Bott–Samelson bimodules.
We closely follow the construction and proofs given in
[
Abe21
]
.
We also provide three main applications of light leaves:

(1)

a version of Soergel’s Hom formula to compute the graded rank of homomorphisms in the category of Bott–Samelson bimodules;

(2)

a basis of the Hom spaces between Bott–Samelson bimodules;

(3)

a cellular structure on Bott–Samelson bimodules.

In order to use the morphism afforded by Proposition
3.4.3
, we will assume throughout this section that
\mathfrak{h}
is a reflection-balanced monodromic Abe realization.

4.1.
Preliminaries on Monodromic Subexpressions

4.1.1.
Subexpressions and Order

Let
\underline{w}=(s_{1},\ldots,s_{k})
be an expression in
W
.
Recall the set,

K(\underline{w},\mathcal{L})=\{1\leq i\leq k\mid\mathcal{L}s_{1}\ldots s_{i}=\mathcal{L}s_{1}\ldots s_{i-1}\}.

We will denote by
\Subexp(\underline{w})
the set of subexpressions of
\underline{w}
.
For a given
x\in W
, we can consider the subset
\Subexp(\underline{w},x)
consisting of subexpressions
\underline{e}
of
\underline{w}
such that
\underline{w}^{\underline{e}}=x
.

A subexpression
\underline{e}=(e_{1},\ldots,e_{k})
of
\underline{w}
is said to be (
\mathcal{L}
-)
monodromic
if
e_{i}=1
whenever
i\notin K(\underline{w},\mathcal{L})
.
We will denote by
\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w})
the subset of
\Subexp(\underline{w})
consisting of
\mathcal{L}
-monodromic subexpressions.
Similarly, for
x\in W
, we will write
\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w},x)=\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w})\cap\Subexp(\underline{w},x)
.

Let
\underline{w}=(s_{1},\ldots,s_{k})\in\Exp(W)
and
\underline{e}\in\Subexp(\underline{w})
.
For each
i=1,\ldots,k
, we write
\underline{w}_{\leq i}
(resp.
\underline{e}_{\leq i}
) for the first
i
terms of
\underline{w}
(resp.
\underline{e}
).
Then
\underline{e}_{\leq i}
is a subexpression of
\underline{w}_{\leq i}
.
Let
w_{i}
be the element expressing
\underline{w}_{\leq i}
.
We can define the
i
-th
label
,
\lab_{i}(\underline{w},\underline{e})\in\{U,D\}
by

\lab_{i}(\underline{w},\underline{e})\coloneq\begin{cases}U&\text{if }w_{i-1}s_{i}>w_{i-1},\\
D&\text{if }w_{i-1}s_{i}<w_{i-1}.\end{cases}

The
i
-th
decoration
of
\underline{e}
, denoted
\dec_{i}(\underline{w},\underline{e})\in\{U0,U1,D0,D1\}
, is defined by

\dec_{i}(\underline{w},\underline{e})\coloneq\lab_{i}(\underline{w},\underline{e})e_{i}.

The
defect
of
\underline{e}
, denoted
d(\underline{w},\underline{e})
, is the integer defined by

d(\underline{w},\underline{e})\coloneq\#\{i\mid\dec_{i}(\underline{w},\underline{e})=U0\}-\#\{i\mid\dec_{i}(\underline{w},\underline{e})=D0\}.

For
x\in W
, we can define a relation
<
, called the
label-lexicographic order
, on
\Subexp(\underline{w},x)
by
\underline{f}<\underline{e}
if and only if there exists some
1\leq i=i(\underline{e},\underline{f})\leq k
such that

(1)

\lab_{j}(\underline{w},\underline{e})=\lab_{j}(\underline{w},\underline{f})
for all
j<i
,

(2)

\lab_{i}(\underline{w},\underline{e})=D
and
\lab_{i}(\underline{w},\underline{f})=U
.

By
[
Abe21
, Lemma 3.9]
, the relation
<
gives a total order on
\Subexp(\underline{w},x)
.
Moreover, if
\underline{e}
and
\underline{f}
are
\mathcal{L}
-monodromic subexpressions, then it follows from the definitions that
i(\underline{e},\underline{f})\in K(\underline{w},\mathcal{L})
.
As a result, the relation
<
restricts to a total order on
\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w},x)
.

We define another relation on subexpressions, although this time without a fixed evaluation.
Let
\underline{e},\underline{f}
be two subexpressions of
\underline{w}\in\Exp(W)
.
Let
x_{0},x_{1},\ldots,x_{m}
and
y_{0},y_{1},\ldots,y_{m}
denote the Bruhat strolls of
\underline{e}
and
\underline{f}
, respectively.
We say that
\underline{e}\prec\underline{f}
if
x_{i}\leq y_{i}
for all
0\leq i\leq m
. This defines a partial order
\prec
on
\Subexp(\underline{w})
called the
path dominance order
.
The path dominance order restricts to a partial order on monodromic subexpressions.

Lemma 4.1.2

(Monodromic Deodhar Defect Formula)
.

Let
\underline{w}\in\Exp(W)
. Then

(4.1.1)

\underline{H}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}=\sum_{\underline{e}\in\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w})}v^{d(\underline{w},\underline{e})}H_{\underline{w}^{\underline{e}}}^{\mathcal{L}}.

As a result, for all
x\in W
, we have

(4.1.2)

p_{\underline{w}}^{x,\mathcal{L}}(v)=\sum_{\underline{e}\in\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w},x)}v^{d(\underline{w},\underline{e})}.

Proof.

Note (
4.1.2
) follows from (
4.1.1
) from the definition of the standard form.
We argue by induction on the length of
\underline{w}
. If
\underline{w}=\varnothing
, then (
4.1.1
) clearly holds.
Let
\underline{w}=\underline{y}s
.
Suppose (
4.1.1
) holds for
\underline{y}
.
Note that for all
x\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
, we have that

H_{x}^{\mathcal{L}}\underline{H}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}=\begin{cases}H_{xs}^{\mathcal{L}}+vH_{x}^{\mathcal{L}}&xs>x,\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s=\mathcal{L}^{\prime},\\
H_{xs}^{\mathcal{L}}+v^{-1}H_{x}^{\mathcal{L}}&xs<x,\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s=\mathcal{L}^{\prime},\\
H_{xs}^{\mathcal{L}}&\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s\neq\mathcal{L}^{\prime}.\end{cases}

If
\mathcal{L}\underline{w}\neq\mathcal{L}\underline{y}
, then any monodromic subexpression of
\underline{w}
arises from a monodromic subexpression of
\underline{y}
by attaching a “1” to the end. In particular, the defect does not change.
We can then compute

\underline{H}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}=\sum_{\underline{e}\in\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{y})}v^{d(\underline{y},\underline{e})}H_{\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}}^{\mathcal{L}}\underline{H}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}\underline{y}}=\sum_{\underline{e}\in\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w})}v^{d(\underline{w},\underline{e})}H_{\underline{w}^{\underline{e}}}^{\mathcal{L}}.

Now assume
\mathcal{L}\underline{w}=\mathcal{L}\underline{y}
. Let
k=\ell(\underline{w})
.

\displaystyle\underline{H}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}

\displaystyle=\sum_{\underline{e}\in\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{y})}v^{d(\underline{y},\underline{e})}H_{\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}}^{\mathcal{L}}\underline{H}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}

\displaystyle=\sum_{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\underline{e}\in\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{y})}}{{\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}s>\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}}}}v^{d(\underline{y},\underline{e})}H_{\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}}^{\mathcal{L}}\underline{H}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}+\sum_{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\underline{e}\in\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{y})}}{{\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}s<\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}}}}v^{d(\underline{y},\underline{e})}H_{\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}}^{\mathcal{L}}\underline{H}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}

\displaystyle=\sum_{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\underline{e}\in\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{y})}}{{\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}s>\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}}}}v^{d(\underline{y},\underline{e})}(H_{\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}s}^{\mathcal{L}}+vH_{\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}})+\sum_{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\underline{e}\in\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{y})}}{{\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}s<\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}}}}v^{d(\underline{y},\underline{e})}(H_{\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}s}^{\mathcal{L}}+v^{-1}H_{\underline{y}^{\underline{e}}})

\displaystyle=\sum_{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\underline{e}\in\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w})}}{{\dec_{k}(\underline{w},\underline{e})=U}}}v^{d(\underline{w},\underline{e})}H_{\underline{w}^{\underline{e}}}^{\mathcal{L}}+\sum_{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\underline{e}\in\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w})}}{{\dec_{k}(\underline{w},\underline{e})=D}}}v^{d(\underline{w},\underline{e})}H_{\underline{w}^{\underline{e}}}^{\mathcal{L}}

\displaystyle=\sum_{\underline{e}\in\Subexp^{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w})}v^{d(\underline{w},\underline{e})}H_{\underline{w}^{\underline{e}}}^{\mathcal{L}}.

∎

4.1.3.
Rigidification Data

As in the non-monodromic setting, the basis of light leaves we will construct is far from canonical.
We define an
\LL
-datum
as a triple (
\rex
,
\{\rex_{s}\}_{s\in S}
,
\{\Gamma_{\underline{x},\underline{y}}\}_{\underline{x},\underline{y}}
) consisting of the following:

(1)

a map
\rex:W\to\Exp(W)
such that for each
x\in W
,
\rex(x)
is a reduced expression for
x
;

(2)

for each
s\in S
, a map
\rex_{s}:\mathscr{R}_{s}\to\Exp(W)
where
\mathscr{R}_{s}=\{w\in W\mid\ell(ws)<\ell(w)\}
and
\rex_{s}(x)
is a reduced expression for
x
ending in
s
;

(3)

for any two reduced expressions
\underline{x}
and
\underline{y}
for
x
, a path
\Gamma_{\underline{x},\underline{y}}
from
\underline{x}
to
\underline{y}
in the rex graph of
x
.

For the remainder of the section, we will fix an
\LL
-datum.

For reduced expressions
\underline{x}
and
\underline{y}
of
x
, we will write
\beta_{\underline{x},\underline{y}}:B_{\underline{x}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to B_{\underline{y}}^{\mathcal{L}}
for the morphism determined by
\Gamma_{\underline{x},\underline{y}}
as in §
3.4
.

4.2.
Definition and Algorithm

Let
\underline{x}=(s_{1},\ldots,s_{k})
be an expression in
W
, and let
\underline{e}
be an
\mathcal{L}
-monodromic subexpression of
\underline{x}
. For each
1\leq i\leq k
, let
x_{i}
be the element realizing
\underline{x}_{\leq i}
.
Let
w_{i}=\underline{w}_{\leq i}^{\underline{e}_{\leq i}}
.
We write
\underline{w}_{i}=\rex(w_{i})
for the reduced expression of
w_{i}
fixed in §
4.1.3
.
The condition that
\underline{e}
be monodromic ensures that
\mathcal{L}x_{i}=\mathcal{L}w_{i}
.

The construction of the light leaves is almost identical to the non-monodromic variants.
The key difference is that we will only allow for monodromic subexpressions.
For the sake of completeness, we will detail the algorithm below.

We construct the light leaf morphism
\LL_{\underline{x},\underline{e}}^{\mathcal{L}}:B_{\underline{x}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}
of degree
d(\underline{x},\underline{e})
inductively on the length
k
of
\underline{x}
.
The base case is covered by defining
\LL_{\varnothing,\varnothing}^{\mathcal{L}}:R\to R
as the identity map.
Suppose that we have already constructed a map

\LL_{i-1}^{\mathcal{L}}:=\LL_{\underline{x}_{\leq i-1},\underline{e}_{\leq i-1}}^{\mathcal{L}}:B_{\underline{x}_{\leq i-1}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to B_{\underline{w}_{i-1}}^{\mathcal{L}}.

In a moment, we will define a map

\phi_{i}:B_{\underline{x}_{\leq i-1}s_{i}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to B_{\underline{w}_{i}}^{\mathcal{L}}.

We then define

\LL_{i}^{\mathcal{L}}=\phi_{i}\circ(\LL_{i-1}^{\mathcal{L}}\otimes_{R}\id_{B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}w_{i-1}}}).

The definition of
\phi_{i}
depends on a decoration
\dec_{i}(\underline{x},\underline{e})
and whether
i\in K(\underline{x},\mathcal{L})
.
We will now explain
\phi_{i}
for each decoration.

(
U0
,
i\in K(\underline{x},\mathcal{L})
):

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi_{i}:B_{\underline{x}_{\leq i-1}}^{\mathcal{L}}\otimes_{R}C_{s_{i}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B_{\underline{x}_{\leq i-1}}^{\mathcal{L}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B_{\underline{w}_{i}}^{\mathcal{L}}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\id\otimes\epsilon^{s_{i}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{\underline{x}_{\leq i-1},\underline{w}_{i}}}

(
U1
,
i\in K(\underline{x},\mathcal{L})
):

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi_{i}:B_{\underline{x}_{\leq i-1}}^{\mathcal{L}}\otimes_{R}C_{s_{i}}=B_{\underline{x}_{\leq i}}^{\mathcal{L}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B_{\underline{w}_{i}}^{\mathcal{L}}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{\underline{x}_{\leq i},\underline{w}_{i}}}

(
U1
,
i\notin K(\underline{x},\mathcal{L})
):

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi_{i}:B_{\underline{x}_{\leq i-1}}^{\mathcal{L}}\otimes_{R}R_{s_{i}}=B_{\underline{x}_{\leq i}}^{\mathcal{L}}}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{\underline{x}_{\leq i},\underline{w}_{i}}}

(
D0
,
i\in K(\underline{x},\mathcal{L})
): Let
\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}}=\rex_{s_{i}}(w_{i})
. We can write
\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}}=\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}}^{\prime}s_{i}
for some reduced expression
\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}}^{\prime}
.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi_{i}:B_{\underline{x}_{\leq i-1}}^{\mathcal{L}}\otimes_{R}C_{s_{i}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{B_{\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}}^{\prime}}^{\mathcal{L}}\otimes_{R}C_{s_{i}}\otimes_{R}C_{s_{i}}}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B_{\underline{w}_{i}}^{\mathcal{L}}.}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}},\underline{w}_{i}}}

(
D1
,
i\in K(\underline{x},\mathcal{L})
): Let
\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}}=\rex_{s_{i}}(w_{i})
. Write
\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}}=\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}}^{\prime}s_{i}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi_{i}:B_{\underline{x}_{\leq i-1}}^{\mathcal{L}}\otimes_{R}C_{s_{i}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{B_{\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}}^{\prime}}^{\mathcal{L}}\otimes_{R}C_{s_{i}}\otimes_{R}C_{s_{i}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{B_{\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}}^{\prime}}^{\mathcal{L}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B_{\underline{w}_{i}}^{\mathcal{L}}.}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}}^{\prime},\underline{w}_{i}}}

(
D1
,
i\notin K(\underline{x},\mathcal{L})
): Let
\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}}=\rex_{s_{i}}(w_{i})
. Write
\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}}=\underline{w}_{i-1,s_{i}}^{\prime}s_{i}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi_{i}:B_{\underline{x}_{\leq i-1}}^{\mathcal{L}}\otimes_{R}R_{s_{i}}}
