6.5.16.
Completing the Proof

Proof of Proposition
6.2.1
.

Let
f:B_{\underline{x}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}
be a diagram of maxwidth
M
.
Since
\ell(\underline{w})<M
, we can write
f=f^{\prime}\circ g_{n}\circ\ldots\circ g_{1}
such that
f^{\prime}
has maxwidth
<M
and each
g_{i}
has height 1 for
1\leq i\leq n
.
By induction, we can replace
f^{\prime}
with a light leaf.
Each
g_{i}
is a generator tensored with identity maps on either side. We can then apply Lemmas
6.5.3
,
6.5.4
,
6.5.5
,
6.5.7
,
6.5.8
,
6.5.9
, and
6.5.11
inductively
to replace
f^{\prime}\circ g_{n}\circ\ldots\circ g_{i}
with a light leaf.
As a result,
f
is in the span of
X_{\underline{x}}^{\mathcal{L}}
modulo
I_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}
.

\square

7.
Geometric Monodromic Hecke Category

The celebrated Riche–Williamson theorem
[
RW18
, Theorem 10.5]
gives a monoidal equivalence of categories

\mathcal{D}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h},W)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}\textnormal{Par}^{\BS}(B\backslash G/B,\mathbbm{k})

from the graded Elias–Williamson diagrammatic category to the category of Bott–Samelson parity sheaves on
B\backslash G/B
where
G
is a complex reductive group and
\mathbbm{k}
is an integral domain.
4
4

4

The Riche–Williamson theorem is in fact more general and holds when
G
is a Kac–Moody group.

In this section, we will establish a monodromic version of the Riche–Williamson theorem using the monodromic diagrammatic category.

Due to issues with choosing representatives of minimal IC sheaves in the (geometric) monodromic Hecke category, we will need to impose some constraints on our coefficient ring (see §
7.2
).
Fix a finite extension
\mathbb{O}
of
\mathbb{Z}_{\ell}
. Denote by
\mathbb{K}
its field of fractions and by
\mathbb{F}
its residue field.
The triple
(\mathbb{K},\mathbb{O},\mathbb{F})
is called an
\ell
-modular triple
. For this section, we will require
\mathbbm{k}\in\{\mathbb{K},\mathbb{O},\mathbb{F}\}
.
Note that
\mathbbm{k}
is either a complete local ring or a field.

7.1.
Preliminaries

7.1.1.
Flag Varieties

Let
G
be a connected complex reductive group. Fix a Borel
B
with Levi decomposition
B=T\ltimes U
.
We denote by
\mathbf{X}
(resp.
\mathbf{Y}
) the character (resp. cocharacter) lattice of
T
.
For any integral domain
\mathbbm{k}
, one can consider the Kac–Moody realization
\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbbm{k}}^{*}=\mathbbm{k}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbf{X}
and
\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbbm{k}}=\mathbbm{k}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbf{Y}
.
Let
(W,S)
denote the Weyl group of
G
with respect to
T
.
For each
s\in S
, there is a simple root
\alpha_{s}\in\mathbf{X}
and a simple coroot
\alpha^{\vee}_{s}\in\mathbf{Y}
.
We often view the simple roots (resp. coroots) as elements of
\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbbm{k}}^{*}
(resp.
\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbbm{k}}
).

Define a ring
\mathbb{Z}^{\prime}
as follows.
If all the maps
\alpha_{s}:\mathbf{Y}\to\mathbb{Z}
and
\alpha_{s}^{\vee}:\mathbf{X}\to\mathbb{Z}
are surjective, we set
\mathbb{Z}^{\prime}=\mathbb{Z}
, and otherwise, we set
\mathbb{Z}^{\prime}=\mathbb{Z}[\frac{1}{2}]
.
For the entirety of this section, we assume that there exists a ring homomorphism
\mathbb{Z}^{\prime}\to\mathbbm{k}
.
The triple
(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbbm{k}},\{\alpha_{s}^{\vee}\}_{s\in S},\{\alpha_{s}\}_{s\in S})
is a reflection-balanced reflection-stable Abe realization (Proposition
2.2.25
and Remark
2.2.31
).
Demazure surjectivity for
\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbbm{k}}
is guaranteed from the ring homomorphism
\mathbb{Z}^{\prime}\to\mathbbm{k}
.
Since multiple coefficient rings will appear throughout this section, we will write
R_{\mathbbm{k}}=\Sym(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbbm{k}}^{*})
instead of
R
to emphasize the dependence on
\mathbbm{k}
.

Let
\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell}\coloneq U\backslash G
denote the enhanced flag variety of
G
. Recall that the Bruhat decomposition

\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell}=\bigsqcup_{w\in W}\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell}_{w}

gives a stratification of
\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell}

where each
\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell}_{w}
is a
B
-orbit (non-canonically) isomorphic to
\mathbb{A}^{\ell(w)}\times T
.
We write
j_{w}:\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell}_{w}\to\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell}
for the inclusion map.

7.1.2.
Hecke Categories

Let
\Ch(T,\mathbbm{k})
denote the set of rank 1 multiplicative local systems on
T
.
A local system
\mathcal{L}\in\Ch(T,\mathbbm{k})
is said to be
torsion
if there exists some
n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}
which is invertible in
\mathbbm{k}
such that
\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}\cong\underline{\mathbbm{k}}_{T}
.
We denote the subset of
\Ch(T,\mathbbm{k})
consisting of torsion local systems by
\Ch^{\mu}(T,\mathbbm{k})
.
We also fix a
W
-orbit
\mathfrak{o}
in
\Ch^{\mu}(T,\mathbbm{k})
.

Let
\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\in\mathfrak{o}
. We can view
\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
as a multiplicative local system on
B
via pullback along
B\to T
.
We can then define the derived category

\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k})\coloneq D_{\cons}(T\backslash_{\mathcal{L}}\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell}/_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}B,\mathbbm{k})

of
(T\times B,\mathcal{L}\boxtimes(\mathcal{L}^{\prime})^{-1})
-equivariant sheaves on
\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell}
. For a precise construction of this category see
[
San25
]
.
As we vary
\mathcal{L}
and
\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
, we can assemble
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k})
into a 2-category, denoted
\>{}_{\backslash}D_{/}(G,\mathbbm{k},\mathfrak{o})
, whose object set is
\mathfrak{o}
, and whose morphism categories are given by
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k})
for
\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\in\mathfrak{o}
.
The horizontal composition in
\>{}_{\backslash}D_{/}(G,\mathbbm{k},\mathfrak{o})
is by the convolution product
\star
(see
[
San25
, §3.3]
).

For each
w\in W
and lift
\dot{w}\in N_{G}(T)
of
w
, by
[
San25
, Proposition 3.2.2]
, there is a perverse
t
-exact equivalence of categories

\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}w}(w,\mathbbm{k})\coloneq D_{\cons}(T\backslash_{\mathcal{L}}\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell}_{w}/_{\mathcal{L}w}B,\mathbbm{k})\cong D_{\cons}(T\backslash\pt,\mathbbm{k})

given by taking the stalk at
\dot{w}
.
We can then define an object
\mathcal{K}_{\dot{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}
in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}w}(w,\mathbbm{k})
as the sheaf corresponding to the constant sheaf in
D_{\cons}(T\backslash\pt,\mathbbm{k})
under the above equivalence.
5
5

5

The notation for objects is opposite to that of
[
San25
]
to match the presentation given for the diagrammatic and algebraic Hecke categories. In particular, in
loc. cit.
,
\mathcal{K}_{\dot{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}
refers to an object with right equivariant monodromy
\mathcal{L}
whereas here it refers to an object with left equivariant monodromy
\mathcal{L}
.

For two different lifts
\dot{w},\dot{w}^{\prime}
of
w
, there is a non-unique isomorphism
\mathcal{K}_{\dot{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}\mathcal{K}_{\dot{w}^{\prime}}^{\mathcal{L}}
.
There are standard, costandard, and simple perverse sheaves defined by

\Delta_{\dot{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}\coloneq j_{w!}\mathcal{K}_{\dot{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}[\ell(w)],\qquad\nabla_{\dot{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}\coloneq j_{w*}\mathcal{K}_{\dot{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}[\ell(w)],\qquad\IC_{\dot{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}=\textnormal{Im}(\Delta_{\dot{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to\nabla_{\dot{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}),

respectively. These are all perverse sheaves in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}w}(G,\mathbbm{k})
. We will frequently replace the
\dot{w}
with
w
in the notation for these sheaves to refer to any object in their isomorphism class rather than a fixed representative.

Remark 7.1.3
.

(1)

There is a canonical representative of
\IC_{e}^{\mathcal{L}}
given by the canonical lift of
e
in
N_{G}(T)
.

(2)

Let
s\in S
such that
\mathcal{L}s=\mathcal{L}
.
Consider the rank 1 Levi subgroup
L_{s}
of
G
corresponding to
s
.
There is a unique extension of
\mathcal{L}
to
L_{s}
, denoted
\mathcal{L}^{s}
(
[
San25
, Lemma 3.2.4]
).
As a result, we have a canonical representative for
\IC_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}
given by
\mathcal{L}^{s}[1]
under the canonical isomorphism
\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell}_{\leq s}\cong U_{s}\backslash L_{s}
where
U_{s}=U\cap L_{s}
.
In particular, when we write
\IC_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}
, we will always refer to the canonical representative of its isomorphism class given here.

Let
\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\in\mathfrak{o}
. There is a forgetful functor

\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{For}:\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k})\to D_{\cons}(\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell}/_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}B,\mathbbm{k})

given by forgetting the left
(T,\mathcal{L})
-equivariance.
We define a full triangulated subcategory

\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\mathbin{\fatbslash}}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k})\subset D_{\cons}(\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell}/_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}B,\mathbbm{k})

generated by the essential image of
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{For}
.
We often abuse notation and regard any object in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k})
as an object in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\mathbin{\fatbslash}}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k})
via
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{For}
.
In particular, the standard, costandard, and IC sheaves can be viewed as objects therein.

7.2.
Minimal IC Sheaves

For each block
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
, there is a minimal element
w^{\beta}
under the partial order
\leq_{\mathcal{L}}
.
We can then consider the perverse sheaf
\IC_{w^{\beta}}^{\mathcal{L}}\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k})
.
A priori, these sheaves are only defined up to (non-unique) isomorphism, and there is no canonical representative of the isomorphism class.
Our first step will be to choose representatives in a coherent manner such that the resulting class is compatible with convolution.
The work in picking these representatives is covered by
[
San25
, §5.8]
.

Let
\Xi^{\mathfrak{o}}(W)
denote the groupoid of blocks. In more detail,
\Xi^{\mathfrak{o}}(W)
is a category whose object set is
\mathfrak{o}
and whose morphism set from
\mathcal{L}
to
\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
is given by
{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
.
In the following proposition, we view
\Xi^{\mathfrak{o}}(W)
as a 2-category by setting all the 2-morphisms to be identities.

Proposition 7.2.1

(
[
San25
, Corollary 5.8.11]
)
.

There exists a 2-functor

\IC_{\min}:\Xi^{\mathfrak{o}}(W)\to\>_{\backslash}D_{/}(G,\mathbbm{k},\mathfrak{o})

taking each
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
to a sheaf in the isomorphism class
\IC_{w^{\beta}}^{\mathcal{L}}
.

We will fix a 2-functor
\IC_{\min}:\Xi^{\mathfrak{o}}(W)\to\>_{\backslash}D_{/}(G,\mathbbm{k},\mathfrak{o})
arising from Proposition
7.2.1
for the remainder of the paper.
It is useful to unpack what this 2-functor entails.
First, for each block
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
, there is an object

\theta_{\beta}^{\mathcal{L}}\coloneq\IC_{\min}(\beta)\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k}).

Second, for each pair of blocks
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
and
\gamma\in{}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}
, there is an isomorphism

b_{\beta,\gamma}:\theta_{\beta}^{\mathcal{L}}\star\theta_{\gamma}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}\theta_{\beta\gamma}^{\mathcal{L}}.

These isomorphisms are associative in the sense that if
\delta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime\prime}}
, there is an equality

b_{\beta\gamma,\delta}(b_{\beta,\gamma}\times\id)=b_{\beta,\gamma\delta}(\id\times b_{\gamma,\delta}).

Remark 7.2.2
.

Proposition
7.2.1
is where we crucially use the assumption that
\mathbbm{k}\in\{\mathbb{K},\mathbb{O},\mathbb{F}\}
.
The reason for this assumption is that the construction of
\IC_{\min}
requires changing the sheaf-theoretic setting to étale sheaves to make use of a Whittaker model.
The author conjectures that such a 2-functor exists under the same assumptions on
\mathbbm{k}
used throughout the paper (namely, noetherian domain of finite global dimension).
If such a 2-functor can be constructed, the rest of our results, namely Theorem
7.8.1
, can be easily derived using similar arguments for these more general coefficient rings.

7.3.
Parity Sheaves

Let
s\in S
and
\mathcal{L}\in\mathfrak{o}
. Let
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}s}
be the block containing
s
.
Define an object in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}s}(G,\mathbbm{k})
by

\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}\coloneq\begin{cases}\IC_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}&\mathcal{L}s=\mathcal{L},\\
\theta_{\beta}^{\mathcal{L}}&\mathcal{L}s\neq\mathcal{L}.\end{cases}

Note that
\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}
comes equipped with a morphism

\epsilon_{s}:\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}\to\theta_{\beta}^{\mathcal{L}}[\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(s)]

defined as the adjunction morphism
\id\to j_{e*}j_{e}^{*}
when
\mathcal{L}s=\mathcal{L}
and
\epsilon_{s}=\id
when
\mathcal{L}s\neq\mathcal{L}
.
More generally, if
\underline{w}=(s_{1},\ldots,s_{k})\in\Exp(W)
, we can define the
Bott–Samelson parity complex
associated to
\underline{w}
by

\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}\coloneq\mathcal{E}_{s_{1}}^{\mathcal{L}}\star\mathcal{E}_{s_{2}}^{\mathcal{L}s_{1}}\star\ldots\star\mathcal{E}_{s_{k}}^{\mathcal{L}s_{1}\ldots s_{k-1}}.

Let
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}\underline{w}}
be the block containing the evaluation of
\underline{w}
, and for each
i=1,\ldots,k
define a block
\beta_{i}\in{}_{\mathcal{L}\underline{w}_{\leq i-1}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}\underline{w}_{\leq i}}
which contains
s_{i}
.
Note that
\beta=\beta_{1}\ldots\beta_{k}
.
We can define a morphism

\epsilon_{\underline{w}}:\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to\theta_{\beta}^{\mathcal{L}}[\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w})]

by the composition

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\beta_{1}}\star\ldots\star\theta^{\mathcal{L}\underline{w}_{\leq k-1}}_{\beta_{k}}[\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w})]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\theta_{\beta}^{\mathcal{L}}[\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(\underline{w})]},}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\epsilon_{s_{1}}\star\ldots\star\epsilon_{s_{k}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim}

where the second map is the canonical isomorphism of minimal IC sheaves arising from
\IC_{\min}
(see Proposition
7.2.1
and the discussion following it).

Define a full subcategory
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(G,\mathbbm{k})
of
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k})
consisting of objects of the form
\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}[n]
for
\underline{w}\in\Exp(W)
with
\mathcal{L}\underline{w}=\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
and
n\in\mathbb{Z}
.
We call
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(G,\mathbbm{k})
the category of
Bott–Samelson parity complexes
. It is clear that convolution preserves Bott–Samelson parity complexes.
As a result, we can define a sub-2-category
\>{}_{\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/}^{\BS}(G,\mathbbm{k},\mathfrak{o})
of
\>{}_{\backslash}D_{/}(G,\mathbbm{k},\mathfrak{o})
whose morphism categories are given by
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(G,\mathbbm{k})
.
We can further consider the idempotent completion of the additive hull of the Bott–Samelson parity complexes, denote by
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k})
.
The objects of
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k})
are called
parity sheaves
.
These categories of parity sheaves can similarly be assembled into a 2-category denoted by
\>{}_{\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/}(G,\mathbbm{k},\mathfrak{o})
.

We will also need the following right-equivariant version of the category of Bott–Samelson parity complexes. Consider the forgetful functor

\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{For}:\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k})\to\>_{\mathcal{L}\mathbin{\fatbslash}}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k}).

Define a full subcategory
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\mathbin{\fatbslash}}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(G,\mathbbm{k})
of
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\mathbin{\fatbslash}}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k})
given by the image of
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{For}
restricted to
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(G,\mathbbm{k})
.
We abuse notation and write
\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}
to refer to the object in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\mathbin{\fatbslash}}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}\underline{w}}^{\BS}(G,\mathbbm{k})
defined by
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{For}(\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}})
.
We will also consider the idempotent completion of the additive hull of
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\mathbin{\fatbslash}}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}^{\BS}(G,\mathbbm{k})
which will be denoted by
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\mathbin{\fatbslash}}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbbm{k})
.

7.4.
Maximal IC Sheaves

For this section, we require that
\mathbbm{k}=\mathbb{K}
so that
\mathbbm{k}
is a field of characteristic 0.
There are variations of the results of this section that hold whenever
\mathbbm{k}=\mathbb{F}
provided certain small primes are invertible.
However, these variations require new proofs that are not provided in
[
San25
]
, and will not be need for the present work.
Note that when
\mathbbm{k}=\mathbb{K}
, the decomposition theorem implies that
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})
is generated under direct sums and shifts by the simple perverse sheaves
\IC_{w}^{\mathcal{L}}
for
w\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}W_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
.

Let
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
be a block. Since
W
is finite, the block
\beta
admits a maximal element
w_{\beta}
under the partial order
\leq_{\beta}
.
We can then consider the perverse sheaf
\IC_{w_{\beta}}^{\mathcal{L}}\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})
. As with the minimal IC sheaves, these sheaves are only defined up to (non-unique) isomorphism.
The goal of the section is two-fold. First, we will use our choices of minimal IC sheaves to fix representatives of the maximal IC sheaves.
Second, we will construct a canonical “coalgebra” structure on the maximal IC sheaves.

7.4.1.
Properties

The following two propositions are mild generalizations of
[
San25
, Proposition 4.4.3]
and
[
San25
, Proposition 4.4.5]
.
Related statements can be found in
[
LY20
, Proposition 6.2]
and
[
LY20
, Proposition 6.4]
.
We omit the proofs as they identical to the referenced propositions.

Proposition 7.4.2
.

Let
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
and
\gamma\in{}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}
.

(1)

The convolution
\IC_{w_{\beta}}^{\mathcal{L}}\star\IC_{w_{\gamma}}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
is isomorphic to a direct sum of shifts of
\IC_{w_{\beta\gamma}}^{\mathcal{L}}
.

(2)

The perverse cohomology
{}^{p}H^{i}\left(\IC_{w_{\beta}}^{\mathcal{L}}\star\IC_{w_{\gamma}}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}\right)=0
unless
-\ell_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(w_{\gamma})\leq i\leq\ell_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(w_{\gamma})
.

(3)

There is an isomorphism

{}^{p}H^{\pm\ell_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(w_{\gamma})}\left(\IC_{w_{\beta}}^{\mathcal{L}}\star\IC_{w_{\gamma}}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}\right)\cong\IC_{w_{\beta\gamma}}^{\mathcal{L}}.

Proposition 7.4.3
.

Let
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
and
w\in\beta
. We have isomorphisms

j_{w}^{*}\IC_{w_{\beta}}^{\mathcal{L}}\cong\mathcal{K}_{w}^{\mathcal{L}}[\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(w_{\beta})+\ell(w)-\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(w)],

j_{w}^{!}\IC_{w_{\beta}}^{\mathcal{L}}\cong\mathcal{K}_{w}^{\mathcal{L}}[-\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(w_{\beta})+\ell(w)+\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(w)].

Definition 7.4.4
.

Let
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
.
A
rigidified maximal IC sheaf
for the block
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
is a pair
(\Theta,\epsilon)
where
\Theta\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})
is such that
\Theta[\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(w_{\beta})]\cong\IC_{w_{\beta}^{\mathcal{L}}}
and
\epsilon:\Theta\to\theta_{\beta}^{\mathcal{L}}
is a nonzero map.

By Proposition
7.4.3
, rigidified maximal IC sheaves exist.
Moreover, there is a unique isomorphism between any two choices of rigidified maximal IC sheaves (cf.,
[
LY20
, 6.5]
).
We can then fix, once-and-for-all, a rigidified maximal IC sheaf
(\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\beta},\epsilon_{\beta})
for each
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
.
When
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}}
is the neutral block, the rigidified maximal IC sheaf will be denoted by
(\Theta_{\circ}^{\mathcal{L}},\epsilon_{\mathcal{L}})
.

7.4.5.
Coalgebra Structure on Maximal IC Sheaves

Let
\Seq^{\mathcal{L}}(W,\mathfrak{o})
denote the set of sequences of composable blocks with left monodromy
\mathcal{L}
.
Explicitly, the
\Seq^{\mathcal{L}}(W,\mathfrak{o})
consists of sequences
\beta_{\bullet}=(\beta_{1},\ldots,\beta_{n})
where
\beta_{i}\in{}_{\mathcal{L}_{i}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}_{i+1}}
for some
\mathcal{L}_{i}\in\mathfrak{o}
such that
\mathcal{L}_{1}=\mathcal{L}
.
For each
\beta_{\bullet}\in\Seq^{\mathcal{L}}(W,\mathfrak{o})
, we write
\pi(\beta_{\bullet})
for the block
\beta_{1}\beta_{2}\ldots\beta_{n}
.
Given
\beta_{\bullet}\in\Seq^{\mathcal{L}}(W,\mathfrak{o})
, we define

\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\star\beta_{\bullet}}=\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta_{1}}\star\ldots\star\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{n}}_{\beta_{n}}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\star\beta_{\bullet}}=\theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta_{1}}\star\ldots\star\theta^{\mathcal{L}_{n}}_{\beta_{n}}.

We also define
\epsilon_{\beta_{\bullet}}:\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\star\beta_{\bullet}}\to\theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\star\beta_{\bullet}}
as the convolution of the various
\epsilon_{\beta_{i}}
’s.

Lemma 7.4.6
.

Let
\beta_{\bullet}\in\Seq^{\mathcal{L}}(W,\mathfrak{o})
.
There is a unique map

\nu_{\beta_{\bullet}}:\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\pi(\beta_{\bullet})}\to\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\star\beta_{\bullet}}

making the following diagram commute,

(7.4.1)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\pi(\beta_{\bullet})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\star\beta_{\bullet}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\pi(\beta_{\bullet})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\star\beta_{\bullet}},}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nu_{\beta_{\bullet}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\epsilon_{\pi(\beta_{\bullet})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\epsilon_{\beta_{\bullet}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim}

where the bottom arrow is the canonical isomorphism for rigidified minimal IC sheaves.

Proof.

By iterating Proposition
7.4.2
, we have that
{}^{p}H^{i}(\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\star\beta_{\bullet}})=0
for
i<0

and
{}^{p}H^{0}(\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\star\beta_{\bullet}})\cong\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\pi(\beta_{\bullet})}
.
Therefore, there is a nonzero map
\nu_{\beta_{\bullet}}:\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\pi(\beta_{\bullet})}\to\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\star\beta_{\bullet}}
.
Note that
\Hom(\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\pi(\beta_{\bullet})},\theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\pi(\beta_{\bullet})})\cong\mathbb{K}
.
As a consequence, if the composition

(7.4.2)

\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\pi(\beta_{\bullet})}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu_{\beta_{\bullet}}}}{{\to}}\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\star\beta_{\bullet}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\epsilon_{\beta_{\bullet}}}}{{\to}}\theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\star\beta_{\bullet}}\cong\theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\pi(\beta_{\bullet})}

is nonzero, then we can rescale
\nu_{\beta_{\bullet}}
to ensure that (
7.4.1
) commutes.

By induction, it suffices to prove (
7.4.2
) is nonzero for
\beta_{\bullet}=(\beta,\gamma)
where
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
and
\gamma\in{}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}
.
Since
\epsilon_{(\beta,\gamma)}=(\epsilon_{\beta}\star\theta_{\gamma}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}})\circ(\id\star\epsilon_{\gamma})
and from Proposition
7.4.2
, we obtain that
{}^{p}H^{0}(\epsilon_{(\beta,\gamma)})
is surjective.
Therefore,
{}^{p}H^{0}(\nu_{(\beta,\gamma)})
is an isomorphism. In particular,
{}^{p}H^{0}(\nu_{(\beta,\gamma)}\circ\epsilon_{(\beta,\gamma)})\neq 0
which proves that (
7.4.2
) is nonzero.
∎

In light of Lemma
7.4.6
, we will write
\nu_{\beta_{\bullet}}:\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\pi(\beta_{\bullet})}\to\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\star\beta_{\bullet}}
for the unique map which satisfies the lemma.
At times, we may simplify the notation and write
\nu=\nu_{\beta_{\bullet}}
.

Proposition 7.4.7
.

Let
\mathcal{L}_{1},\mathcal{L}_{2},\mathcal{L}_{3},\mathcal{L}_{4}\in\mathfrak{o}
and
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}_{1}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}_{2}}
,
\gamma\in{}_{\mathcal{L}_{2}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}_{3}}
,
\delta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}_{3}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}_{4}}
.
The following diagrams commute

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta\gamma\delta}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta}\star\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{2}}_{\gamma\delta}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta\gamma}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta}\star\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{2}}_{\gamma}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta}\star\theta^{\mathcal{L}_{2}}_{\gamma}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta\gamma}\star\Theta_{\mathcal{L}_{3}}^{\delta}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta}\star\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{2}}_{\gamma}\star\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{3}}_{\delta},}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta}\star\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{2}}_{\gamma}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta}\star\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{2}}_{\gamma}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta\gamma}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nu}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nu}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\id\star\nu}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nu}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nu}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\id}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\id\star\epsilon}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nu\star\id}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\epsilon\star\id}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim}

Proof.

The first diagram commutes by the uniqueness of
\nu_{(\beta,\gamma,\delta)}
from Lemma
7.4.6
.
For the second diagram, we can compose

(7.4.3)

\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta\gamma}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{\to}}\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta}\star\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{2}}_{\gamma}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\epsilon_{\beta}\star\id}}{{\to}}\theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta}\star\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{2}}_{\gamma}\cong\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta\gamma}

with
\epsilon_{\beta\gamma}
.
The defining property (
7.4.1
) for
\nu
ensures that this composition is
\epsilon_{\beta\gamma}
.
Since
\End(\Theta^{\mathcal{L}_{1}}_{\beta\gamma})\cong\mathbb{K}
, we may conclude that (
7.4.3
) is the identity map. The other triangle in the second diagram commutes by a similar argument.
∎

7.5.
Soergel Functor

We keep the assumption from the previous section that
\mathbbm{k}=\mathbb{K}
.

Let
\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})
. The internal sheaf Hom object
\textbf{R}\mathcal{H}om(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})
is naturally a
B
-biequivariant sheaf on
G
,
Moreover, there is an isomorphism

\Hom_{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})}^{\bullet}(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})\coloneq\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\Hom_{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})}(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}[n])\cong H_{T\times T}^{\bullet}(\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell},\textbf{R}\mathcal{H}om(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})).

As a result, there is an action of
R_{\mathbb{K}}\cong H_{T}^{\bullet}(\pt;\mathbb{K})
on both the left and right of
\Hom^{\bullet}(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})
which makes
\Hom^{\bullet}(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})
into a graded
R_{\mathbb{K}}
-bimodule.

Let
\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\in\mathfrak{o}
, and write
\Theta^{[\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime}]}\coloneq\bigoplus_{\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}}\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\beta}.

We define the Soergel
\mathbb{H}
-functor,

\mathbb{H}:\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})\to R_{\mathbb{K}}\textnormal{-bim}^{\mathbb{Z}},\qquad\mathcal{F}\mapsto\Hom_{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})}^{\bullet}(\Theta^{[\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime}]},\mathcal{F}).

We will also consider a “right-equivariant” version of the Soergel functor.

\tilde{\mathbb{H}}:\>_{\mathcal{L}\mathbin{\fatbslash}}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})\to\textnormal{mod}^{\mathbb{Z}}\textnormal{-}R_{\mathbb{K}},\qquad\mathcal{F}\mapsto\Hom_{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\mathbin{\fatbslash}}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})}^{\bullet}(\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{For}(\Theta^{[\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime}]}),\mathcal{F}).

7.5.1.
Behavior on Objects

We recall some facts about the
\mathbb{H}
-functor from
[
LY20
]
or
[
San25
]
.

Lemma 7.5.2

(
[
LY20
, Lemma 7.3]
)
.

There is a canonical isomorphism in
R_{\mathbb{K}}\textnormal{-bim}^{\mathbb{Z}}

\mathbb{H}(\theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\beta})\cong R_{w^{\beta}}

under which the canonical map
\epsilon^{\beta}:\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\beta}\to\theta_{\beta}^{\mathcal{L}}
corresponds to
1\in R_{w^{\beta}}
.

If
\mathcal{L}s=\mathcal{L}
, by
[
San25
, Lemma 4.5.6]
, then there is a unique map
\xi_{s}:\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\circ}\to\IC_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}[-1]
making the following diagram commute,

(7.5.1)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Theta^{\mathcal{L}}_{\circ}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\IC_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}[-1]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\IC_{e}^{\mathcal{L}},}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\xi_{s}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\epsilon_{\mathcal{L}}}

where the right downwards arrow is induced from the unit of the adjunction
\id\to j_{e*}j_{e}^{*}
.

Lemma 7.5.3

(
[
LY20
, Lemma 7.4]
)
.

Let
s\in S
and
\mathcal{L}\in\mathfrak{o}
such that
\mathcal{L}s=\mathcal{L}
.

(1)

Let
\mathcal{F}\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})
.
There is a canonical isomorphism in
R_{\mathbb{K}}\textnormal{-bim}^{\mathbb{Z}}
,

(7.5.2)

\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F})\otimes_{R^{s}}R(1)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F}\star\IC_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}).

(2)

There is a canonical isomorphism in
R_{\mathbb{K}}\textnormal{-bim}^{\mathbb{Z}}

(7.5.3)

\mathbb{H}(\IC_{s}^{\mathcal{L}})\cong C_{s}

under which the map
\xi_{s}:\Theta_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ}\to\IC_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}[-1]
corresponds to
u_{s}\in C_{s}
.

7.5.4.
2-Cateorical Structure

Let
R_{\mathbb{K}}\textnormal{-bim}^{\mathbb{Z}}_{\mathfrak{o}}
denote the 2-category whose object set is
\mathfrak{o}
and where each morphism category is a copy of
R_{\mathbb{K}}\textnormal{-bim}^{\mathbb{Z}}
.
The horizontal composition is given by the tensor product of graded
R_{\mathbb{K}}
-bimodules.
By Proposition
7.4.7
, the Soergel
\mathbb{H}
-functor extends to a lax 2-functor

\mathbb{H}:\>_{\backslash}D_{/}(G,\mathbb{K},\mathfrak{o})\to R_{\mathbb{K}}\textnormal{-bim}^{\mathbb{Z}}_{\mathfrak{o}}

It is useful to unpack what the (lax) 2-functor condition means here.
Let
\mathcal{F}\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})
and
\mathcal{G}\in\>_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})
.
We have maps

\displaystyle\Hom(\Theta^{[\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime}]},\mathcal{F}[i])\times\Hom(\Theta^{[\mathcal{L}^{\prime},\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}]},\mathcal{G}[j])

\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\star}}{{\to}}\Hom(\Theta^{[\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime}]}\star\Theta^{[\mathcal{L}^{\prime},\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}]},\mathcal{F}\star\mathcal{G}[i+j])

\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle(-)\circ\nu}}{{\longrightarrow}}\Hom(\Theta^{[\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}]},\mathcal{F}\star\mathcal{G}[i+j]),

where
\nu:\Theta^{[\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}]}\to\Theta^{[\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime}]}\star\Theta^{[\mathcal{L}^{\prime},\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}]}
is given by summing over all

\nu_{(\beta,\gamma)}:\Theta_{\beta\gamma}^{\mathcal{L}}\to\Theta_{\beta}^{\mathcal{L}}\star\Theta_{\gamma}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}

for
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
and
\gamma\in{}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}
.
This map factors through a morphism of graded
R_{\mathbb{K}}
-bimodules,

c(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}):\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F})\otimes_{R}\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G})\to\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F}\star\mathcal{G})

which produce natural transformations

c:\mathbb{H}(-)\otimes_{R}\mathbb{H}(-)\implies\mathbb{H}(-\star-):\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})\times\>_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})\to R_{\mathbb{K}}\textnormal{-bim}^{\mathbb{Z}}.

From here, one can observe that
\mathbb{H}
is a lax 2-functor from Proposition
7.4.7
(cf.,
[
LY20
, §7.5]
).
Our goal is to show that on parity sheaves, the natural transformation
c
is an equivalence.
The following is a combination of
[
LY20
, Lemma 7.6]
and
[
LY20
, Lemma 7.7]
(also see
[
San25
, Lemma 4.5.8]
).

Lemma 7.5.5
.

Let
\mathcal{F}\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}D_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})
,
\gamma\in{}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}^{\prime\prime}}
, and
s\in S
.

(1)

The morphism
c(\mathcal{F},\theta^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}_{\gamma})
is an isomorphism.

(2)

If
\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s=\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
, then the morphism
c(\mathcal{F},\IC_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}})
is an isomorphism.

Corollary 7.5.6
.

The restriction of the lax 2-functor
\mathbb{H}
to parity sheaves,

\mathbb{H}:\>_{\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/}(G,\mathbb{K},\mathfrak{o})\to R_{\mathbb{K}}\textnormal{-bim}^{\mathbb{Z}}_{\mathfrak{o}},

is a (strong) 2-functor.

Proof.

By induction using Lemma
7.5.5
, the morphisms
c(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})
are isomorphisms whenever
\mathcal{F}
and
\mathcal{G}
are Bott–Samelson parity complexes.
The result then follows by taking direct summands using the classification of parity sheaves from
[
San25
, Theorem 3.4.1]
.
∎

7.5.7.
Equivalence with Soergel Bimodules

Define a 2-category
\>{}_{\backslash}\!\!{}^{\circ}\mathcal{A}_{/}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{K}},W,\mathfrak{o})
whose object set is
\mathfrak{o}
. The 1-morphisms in
\>{}_{\backslash}\!\!{}^{\circ}\mathcal{A}_{/}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{K}},W,\mathfrak{o})
are given by symbols
M(n)
where
M
is a 1-morphism in
\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{K}},W,\mathfrak{o})
and
n\in\mathbb{Z}
.
The 2-morphisms from
M(m)
to
M(n)
are the 2-morphisms
M\to N
of degree
n-m
in
\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{K}},W,\mathfrak{o})
. The horizontal and vertical compositions are those inherited from
\>{}_{\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{K}},W,\mathfrak{o})
.
Note that on morphism categories, using the notation of Appendix
B
,
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\!\!{}^{\circ}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{K}},W,\mathfrak{o})=\left(\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{K}},W,\mathfrak{o})\right)^{\circ}
.

Since
\mathbb{K}
is a characteristic 0 field, it contains a copy of
\mathbb{Q}
. The Kac–Moody realization of
W
over
\mathbb{Q}
is a faithful
W
-representation, and hence, we must have that
\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{K}}
is also faithful.
As a result, by Lemma
3.1.4
, the forgetful 2-functor

\>{}_{\backslash}\!\!{}^{\circ}\mathcal{A}_{/}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{K}},W,\mathfrak{o})\to R_{\mathbb{K}}\textnormal{-bim}^{\mathbb{Z}}_{\mathfrak{o}}

is locally fully faithful. By Lemma
7.5.2
, Lemma
7.5.3
, and Corollary
7.5.6
, we then have that
\mathbb{H}
-functor factors through a 2-functor

\mathbb{H}:\>_{\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/}(G,\mathbb{K},\mathfrak{o})\to\>_{\backslash}\!\!{}^{\circ}\mathcal{A}_{/}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{K}},W,\mathfrak{o}).

We are ready to state the main result of the section.

Theorem 7.5.8
.

The
\mathbb{H}
-functor restricts to an equivalence of 2-categories

\mathbb{H}:\>_{\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/}(G,\mathbb{K},\mathfrak{o})\to\>_{\backslash}\!\!{}^{\circ}\mathcal{A}_{/}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{K}},W,\mathfrak{o})

such that
\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}[n])\cong B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}(n)
for all
\underline{w}\in\Exp(W)
,
\mathcal{L}\in\mathfrak{o}
, and
n\in\mathbb{Z}
.

Corollary 7.5.9
.

Let
\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\in\mathfrak{o}
. The
\tilde{\mathbb{H}}
-functor restricts to a fully faithful functor

\tilde{\mathbb{H}}:\>_{\mathcal{L}\mathbin{\fatbslash}}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})\to\textnormal{mod}^{\mathbb{Z}}\textnormal{-}R_{\mathbb{K}}

such that
\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}[n])\cong B_{w}^{\mathcal{L}}(n)
for all
\underline{w}\in\Exp(W)
and
n\in\mathbb{Z}
such that
\mathcal{L}\underline{w}=\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
.
Moreover, we have that
\tilde{\mathbb{H}}
is related to
\mathbb{H}
by the following diagram which commutes up to natural isomorphism,

(7.5.4)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\!\!{}^{\circ}\mathcal{A}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{K}},W,\mathfrak{o})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\mathbin{\fatbslash}}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\textnormal{mod}^{\mathbb{Z}}\textnormal{-}R_{\mathbb{K}}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{For}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{H}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{K}\otimes_{R_{\mathbb{K}}}(-)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\tilde{\mathbb{H}}}

Proof.

The first part of the corollary follows from Theorem
7.5.8
using the same argument as
[
San25
, Proposition 4.7.1]
.
Diagram (
7.5.4
) commutes by
[
San25
, Lemma 3.6.5]
and Theorem
4.6.2
.
∎

It is clear from Lemma
7.5.2
and Lemma
7.5.3
that
\mathbb{H}
is locally essentially surjective.
As a result, to prove Theorem
7.5.8
, it suffices to show that
\mathbb{H}
is locally fully faithful.
Before proving full faithfulness, we need some preliminary lemmas.

Lemma 7.5.10
.

Let
\mathcal{G}\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})
. The natural map

\Hom(\IC_{e}^{\mathcal{L}},\mathcal{G})\to\Hom(R,\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G}))

induced by
\mathbb{H}
is an isomorphism.

Proof.

The lemma follows from the proof of
[
LY20
, Lemma 7.10]
after the obvious modifications are made.
∎

Lemma 7.5.11
.

Let
s\in S
,
\mathcal{F}\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})
, and
\mathcal{G}\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}(G,\mathbb{K})
. There is a natural commutative diagram

(7.5.5)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathcal{F}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}},\mathcal{G})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}),\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F}),\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F})\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}},\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F}),\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G})\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{H}}

where the horizontal maps are given by the self-adjunction of
(-)\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
and
(-)\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}
.

Proof.

We can factor the diagram (

) as follows:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathcal{F}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}},\mathcal{G})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathcal{F}\star\mathcal{E}_{(s,s)}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}},\mathcal{G}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}),\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F}\star\mathcal{E}_{(s,s)}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}),\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F}),\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F})\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}},\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F})\otimes_{R}B_{(s,s)}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}},\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G})\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F}),\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G})\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{H}}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{H}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{H}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(-)\circ c(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{H}(-\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c(\mathcal{G},\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s})^{-1}\circ(-)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(-)\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}}

where the horizontal morphisms on the right are given by unit morphisms of adjunctions.
The top two squares commute by functorality of
\mathbb{H}
. The bottom two squares commute by Corollary
7.5.6
.
∎

Proof of Theorem
7.5.8
.

Let
\mathcal{L},\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\in\mathfrak{o}
and
\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})
.
Consider the morphism

\alpha(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}):\Hom(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})\to\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{F}),\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G}))

Since every sheaf in
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}(G,\mathbb{K})
is in the idempotent completion of the additive hull of the Bott–Samelson sheaves it suffices to
prove that
\alpha(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})
is an isomorphism for
\mathcal{F}=\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}
for all expressions
\underline{w}=(s_{1},\ldots,s_{k})\in\Exp(W)
with
\mathcal{L}\underline{w}=\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
.
We will prove
\alpha(\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}},\mathcal{G})
is an isomorphism by induction on
k
. The base case of
w=e
is covered by Lemma

7.5.10
.

Let
s=s_{k}
.
By Lemma
7.5.11
, we get a commutative diagram

(7.5.6)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}_{\leq k-1}}^{\mathcal{L}}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s},\mathcal{G})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}_{\leq k-1}}^{\mathcal{L}},\mathcal{G}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}_{\leq k-1}}^{\mathcal{L}}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s}),\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}_{\leq k-1}}^{\mathcal{L}}),\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}_{\leq k-1}}^{\mathcal{L}})\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}s},\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\Hom(\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}_{\leq k-1}}^{\mathcal{L}}),\mathbb{H}(\mathcal{G})\otimes_{R}B_{s}^{\mathcal{L}^{\prime}})}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{H}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{H}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim}
7.5.6
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim}
7.5.6
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim}

The top right vertical map is an isomorphism by induction; therefore, we must have that
\alpha(\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}},\mathcal{G})

is an isomorphism. We can then conclude that
\mathbb{H}
is locally fully faithful.

\square

7.6.
Constructing the Riche–Williamson Functor

Lemma 7.6.1
.

Let
\mathbbm{k},\mathbbm{k}^{\prime}
be noetherian domains of finite global dimension, and let
\varphi:\mathbbm{k}\to\mathbbm{k}^{\prime}
be a ring homomorphism.
Let
\mathcal{L}\in\Ch^{\mu}(T,\mathbbm{k})
.
For all
w\in W
, one has that
\mathcal{L}w=\mathcal{L}
if and only if
\mathbbm{k}^{\prime}(\mathcal{L})w=\mathbbm{k}^{\prime}(\mathcal{L})
.

Proof.

If
\mathcal{L}w=\mathcal{L}
, then clearly
\mathbbm{k}^{\prime}(\mathcal{L})w=\mathbbm{k}^{\prime}(\mathcal{L})
since
\mathbbm{k}^{\prime}(-)
commutes with the
W
-action.
Now suppose that
\mathbbm{k}^{\prime}(\mathcal{L})w=\mathbbm{k}^{\prime}(\mathcal{L})

There exists some
n\in\mathbb{Z}
invertible in
\mathbbm{k}
such that
\mathcal{L}
is defined by a group homomorphism

\rho_{\mathcal{L}}:\mathbf{Y}\to\mu_{n}(\mathbbm{k})

where
\mu_{n}(\mathbbm{k})
is the group of
n
-th roots of unity in
\mathbbm{k}
. By assumption, we have that for all
\lambda\in\mathbf{Y}
,

\varphi(\rho_{\mathcal{L}}(\lambda\cdot w-\lambda))=1.

In other words,
\rho_{\mathcal{L}}(\lambda\cdot w-\lambda)
is in the kernel of the group homomorphism
\mu_{n}(\mathbbm{k})\to\mu_{n}(\mathbbm{k}^{\prime})
.
We claim that
\mu_{n}(\mathbbm{k})\to\mu_{n}(\mathbbm{k}^{\prime})
is injective. Let
\zeta\in\mu_{n}(\mathbbm{k})
such that
\varphi(\zeta)=1
.
Assume that
\zeta\neq 1
. Since
\mathbbm{k}
is a domain and
\zeta^{n}-1=0
, we must have that
\zeta^{n-1}+\zeta^{n-2}+\ldots+1=0
.
We can then compute

0=\varphi(\zeta^{n-1}+\zeta^{n-2}+\ldots+1)=\varphi(\zeta)^{n-1}+\varphi(\zeta)^{n-2}+\ldots+\varphi(1)=n.

However,
n
is assumed to be invertible in
\mathbbm{k}
and hence also in
\mathbbm{k}^{\prime}
, so this contradicts our assumption that
\zeta\neq 1
.
We conclude that
\rho_{\mathcal{L}}(\lambda\cdot w-\lambda)=1
which translates into the condition that
\mathcal{L}w=\mathcal{L}
.
∎

We return to the general case where
\mathbbm{k}\in\{\mathbb{K},\mathbb{O},\mathbb{F}\}
with ring homomorphism
\mathbb{Z}^{\prime}\to\mathbbm{k}
.

For each
\mathcal{L}\in\mathfrak{o}
, we can find some
\mathcal{L}_{\mathbb{O}}\in\Ch^{\mu}(T,\mathbb{O})
such that
\mathbbm{k}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathbb{O}})\cong\mathcal{L}
.
Indeed, if
\mathbbm{k}=\mathbb{F}
, this follows from the existence of a Teichmüller lift
\mathbb{F}^{\times}\to\mathbb{O}^{\times}
. For
\mathbbm{k}=\mathbb{K}
, this can be constructed using the fact that the roots of unity of
\mathbb{K}
are contained in
\mathbb{O}
.
Define
\mathfrak{o}_{\mathbb{O}}=\mathcal{L}_{\mathbb{O}}\cdot W
for some
\mathcal{L}\in\mathfrak{o}
. We can then set
\mathfrak{o}_{\mathbb{K}}=\mathbb{K}(\mathcal{L}_{O})\cdot W
and
\mathfrak{o}_{\mathbb{F}}=\mathbb{F}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathbb{O}})
.
Note that
\mathfrak{o}_{\mathbbm{k}}=\mathfrak{o}
.
For
\mathcal{L}\in\mathfrak{o}
, the sheaf
\mathcal{L}_{\mathbb{O}}
is torsion, and hence
\mathfrak{o}_{\mathbbm{k}}\subseteq\Ch^{\mu}(T,\mathbbm{k})
.
By Lemma
7.6.1
, extension of scalars
\mathbbm{k}(-):\mathfrak{o}_{\mathbb{O}}\to\mathfrak{o}_{\mathbbm{k}}
gives a
W
-equivariant bijection.
We can then abuse notation and simply write
\mathfrak{o}
to refer to any
\mathfrak{o}_{\mathbbm{k}}
with
\mathbbm{k}\in\{\mathbb{K},\mathbb{O},\mathbb{F}\}
under these bijections.
Likewise, for any
\mathcal{L}\in\mathfrak{o}
, we will simultaneously view it as an object in
\mathfrak{o}_{\mathbbm{k}}
for any such
\mathbbm{k}
.
Moreover, extension of scalars defines a 2-functor

\mathbbm{k}(-):\>_{\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/}^{\BS}(G,\mathbb{O},\mathfrak{o})\to\>_{\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/}^{\BS}(G,\mathbbm{k},\mathfrak{o}).

Recall the 2-category
\>{}_{\backslash}\!\!{}^{\circ}\mathcal{D}_{/}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbbm{k}},W,\mathfrak{o})
constructed in §
5.7.11
.
The goal of this section is to construct a 2-functor

\Upsilon_{\textnormal{RW}}^{\mathbbm{k}}:\>_{\backslash}\!\!{}^{\circ}\mathcal{D}_{/}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbbm{k}},W,\mathfrak{o})\to\>_{\backslash}\textnormal{Par}_{/}^{\BS}(G,\mathbbm{k},\mathfrak{o}).

The construction is analogous to the non-monodromic version constructed by Riche and Williamson
[
RW18
]
.
We will first define
\Upsilon_{\RW}^{\mathbb{O}}
. We will then check that the defining relations in
\>{}_{\backslash}\!\!{}^{\circ}\mathcal{D}_{/}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{K}},W,\mathfrak{o})
are satisfied by extending scalars of
\Upsilon_{\RW}^{\mathbb{O}}
to
\mathbb{K}
-coefficients.
Finally, we will extend scalars to construct
\Upsilon_{\RW}^{\mathbb{F}}
.

It is easy to define
\Upsilon_{\RW}^{\mathbb{O}}
on 1-morphisms. For an expression
\underline{w}\in\Exp(W)
,
\mathcal{L}\in\mathfrak{o}
, and
n\in\mathbb{Z}
, we define

\Upsilon_{\RW}^{\mathbb{O}}(B_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}(n))\coloneq\mathcal{E}_{\underline{w}}^{\mathcal{L}}[n]\in\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\!\!{}^{\circ}\mathcal{D}_{/\mathcal{L}\underline{w}}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{O}},W,\mathfrak{o}).

We then must specify the image of the generating 2-morphisms in
\>{}_{\backslash}\!\!{}^{\circ}\mathcal{D}_{/}^{\BS}(\mathfrak{h}_{\mathbb{O}},W,\mathfrak{o})
.

7.6.2.
Polynomials

Let
\mathcal{L}\in\mathfrak{o}
.
Since
\mathcal{E}_{\varnothing}^{\mathcal{L}}=\IC_{e}^{\mathcal{L}}=\Delta_{e}^{\mathcal{L}}
, by adjunction, we have a canonical isomorphism,

\xi:\End^{\bullet}(\mathcal{E}_{\varnothing}^{\mathcal{L}})\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}H_{T}^{\bullet}(\pt;\mathbb{O})=R_{\mathbb{O}}.

7.6.3.
1-color morphisms

Let
s\in S
and
\mathcal{L}\in\mathfrak{o}
such that
\mathcal{L}s=\mathcal{L}
.
By
[
San25
, Lemma 4.3.7]
, the object
\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}
carries a graded Frobenius algebra structure with structure maps

\mu_{s}:\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}\to\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}[-1],\qquad\nu_{s}:\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}\to\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}[-1],

\eta_{s}:\IC_{e}^{\mathcal{L}}\to\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}[1],\qquad\epsilon_{s}:\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}\to\IC_{e}^{\mathcal{L}}[1],

where
\epsilon_{s}
is the map defined in §
7.3
and
\eta_{s}
is defined by the adjunction counit
j_{e*}j_{e}^{!}\to\id
.

Now let
s\in S
and
\mathcal{L}\in\mathfrak{o}
such that
\mathcal{L}s\neq\mathcal{L}
. By Proposition
7.2.1
, we have a canonical isomorphism of minimal IC sheaves
\cap_{s}:\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}}\star\mathcal{E}_{s}^{\mathcal{L}s}\to\IC_{e}^{\mathcal{L}}
with inverse
\cup_{s}
.
We can then define

\Upsilon_{\RW}^{\mathbb{O}}\left(\hbox to29.45pt{\vbox to29.45pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 14.72638pt\lower-14.72638pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@closescope \lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \hbox to0.0pt{

7.6.4.
2
m_{s,t}
-valent vertices

Let
s,t\in S
be distinct simple reflections and
\mathcal{L}\in\mathfrak{o}
. Define
m=m_{s,t}
and
w={}_{s}m={}_{t}m
.

Lemma 7.6.5
.

We use the same notation as above. The pullback
j_{w}^{*}
induces an isomorphism of
\mathbb{O}
-modules

(7.6.1)

\Hom(\mathcal{E}_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}},\mathcal{E}_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}})\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}\Hom(j_{w}^{*}\mathcal{E}_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}},j_{w}^{*}\mathcal{E}_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}).

Moreover, both sides of (
7.6.1
) are free
\mathbb{O}
-modules of rank 1.

Proof.

The lemma is essentially a variation of
[
San25
, Lemma 5.4.4]
. By the Soergel Hom formula for the monodromic Hecke category (see
[
San25
, Proposition 3.8.13]
), there is an isomorphism
\Hom(\mathcal{E}_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}},\mathcal{E}_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}})\cong\mathbb{O}
.
By the same argument as in
[
San25
, Theorem 3.4.1]
, we have an isomorphism
j_{w}^{*}\mathcal{E}_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\cong\mathcal{K}_{w}^{\mathcal{L}}[\ell_{\mathcal{L}}(w)]\cong j_{w}^{*}\mathcal{E}_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}
. Moreover,
\End(\mathcal{K}_{w}^{\mathcal{L}})\cong\mathbb{O}
.
Since
\widetilde{\mathcal{F}\ell}_{w}
is open in the support of
\mathcal{E}_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}
and
\mathcal{E}_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}
, we have that the map (
7.6.1
) is surjective.
Both sides of (
7.6.1
) are free of rank 1; therefore, (
7.6.1
) is an isomorphism.
∎

Define the map
g_{s,t}:\mathcal{E}_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to\mathcal{E}_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}
as the pre-image under (
7.6.1
) of an isomorphism
f_{s,t}^{w}:j_{w}^{*}\mathcal{E}_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}j_{w}^{*}\mathcal{E}_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}
.
Likewise, by switching the roles of
s
and
t
, there is a map
g_{t,s}:\mathcal{E}_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to\mathcal{E}_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}
lifted from an isomorphism
g_{t,s}^{w}:j_{w}^{*}\mathcal{E}_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\to}}j_{w}^{*}\mathcal{E}_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}
.
We pick
g_{s,t}^{w}
and
g_{t,s}^{w}
such that
g_{t,s}^{w}\circ g_{s,t}^{w}=\id_{j_{w}^{*}\mathcal{E}_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}}
.

To define the image of the
2m_{s,t}
-valent vertices, we will need another lemma.

Lemma 7.6.6
.

We use the same notation as above. Let
\beta\in{}_{\mathcal{L}}\underline{W}_{\mathcal{L}w}
be the block containing
w
. For
u\in\{s,t\}
, we have

\Hom_{\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\mathbin{\fatbslash}}D_{/\mathcal{L}w}(G,\mathbb{O})}(\mathcal{E}_{{}_{u}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}},\theta_{\beta}^{\mathcal{L}}[m])=\mathbb{O}\cdot\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{For}(\epsilon_{{}_{u}\underline{m}}).

Proof.

By
[
San25
, Lemma 3.6.5]
and
[
San25
, Proposition 3.8.13]
, the space in question is free of rank 1 over
\mathbb{O}
.
It then suffices to show that
\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{For}(\epsilon_{{}_{u}\underline{m}})
is nonzero after extension of scalars to any field. This is clear since extension of scalars commutes with convolution and the unit of the adjunction
\id\to j_{s*}j_{s}^{*}
for any
s\in S_{\mathcal{L}}^{\circ}
.
∎

By Lemma
7.6.6
, we have

(7.6.2)

\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{For}(\epsilon_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}\circ g_{s,t})=c_{s,t}\cdot\left(\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{For}(\epsilon_{{}_{s}\underline{m}})\right)\qquad\text{and}\qquad\>_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{For}(\epsilon_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}\circ g_{t,s})=c_{t,s}\cdot\left(\>{}_{\mathcal{L}\backslash}\textnormal{For}(\epsilon_{{}_{t}\underline{m}})\right)

for some
c_{s,t},c_{t,s}\in\mathbb{O}
. We can now set

f_{s,t}\coloneq c_{t,s}g_{s,t}:\mathcal{E}_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to\mathcal{E}_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\qquad\text{and}\qquad f_{t,s}\coloneq c_{s,t}g_{t,s}:\mathcal{E}_{{}_{t}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}}\to\mathcal{E}_{{}_{s}\underline{m}}^{\mathcal{L}},

and then define these to be the image of the
2m
-valent vertices under
\Upsilon_{\RW}^{\mathbb{O}}
:

\Upsilon_{\RW}^{\mathbb{O}}\left(\hbox to57.91pt{\vbox to57.91pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 28.95276pt\lower-28.95276pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@closescope \lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \hbox to0.0pt{
{
{}{}{}}{}{{}}{}{
{}{}{}}
{}{}\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{}\lxSVG@stroke\lxSVG@drawpath@unclipped{M -32.87 -39.37 L 0 0}{fill:none} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces
\lxSVG@closescope {
{}{}{}}{}{{}}{}{
{}{}{}}
{}{}\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{}\lxSVG@stroke\lxSVG@drawpath@unclipped{M -6.5 -39.37 L 0 0}{fill:none} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces
\lxSVG@closescope {

{}{}\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{}\lxSVG@stroke\lxSVG@drawpath@unclipped{M 0 0 L -19.69 39.37}{fill:none} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces
\lxSVG@closescope {

\lxSVG@closescope {

\lxSVG@closescope {

{}{}\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{}\lxSVG@stroke\lxSVG@drawpath@unclipped{M 0 0 L -6.5 39.37}{fill:none} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces
\lxSVG@closescope {
